    59→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
    60→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
    61→
    62→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
    63→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
    64→    """
    65→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
    66→
    67→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files.
    68→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
    69→        before = len(functions)
    70→        functions = [
    71→            f
    72→            for f in functions
    73→            if lang.zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES
    74→        ]
    75→        excluded = before - len(functions)
    76→        if excluded:
    77→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
    78→
    79→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
    80→    findings = make_dupe_findings(entries, log)
    81→    return findings, {"dupes": total_functions}
    82→
    83→
    84→def phase_boilerplate_duplication(
    85→    path: Path,
    86→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    87→) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
    88→    """Shared phase runner: detect repeated boilerplate code via jscpd."""
    89→    entries = detect_with_jscpd(path)
    90→    if entries is None:
    91→        return [], {}
    92→    entries = _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries, lang.zone_map)
    93→
    94→    findings: list[Finding] = []
    95→    for entry in entries:
    96→        locations = entry["locations"]
    97→        first = locations[0]
    98→        loc_preview = ", ".join(
    99→            f"{rel(item['file'])}:{item['line']}" for item in locations[:4]
   100→        )
   101→        if len(locations) > 4:
   102→            loc_preview += f", +{len(locations) - 4} more"
   103→        findings.append(
   104→            make_finding(
   105→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   106→                first["file"],
   107→                entry["id"],
   108→                tier=3,
   109→                confidence="medium",
   110→                summary=(
   111→                    f"Boilerplate block repeated across {entry['distinct_files']} files "
   112→                    f"(window {entry['window_size']} lines): {loc_preview}"
   113→                ),
   114→                detail={
   115→                    "distinct_files": entry["distinct_files"],
   116→                    "window_size": entry["window_size"],
   117→                    "locations": locations,
   118→                    "sample": entry["sample"],
   119→                },
   120→            )
   121→        )
   122→
   123→    if findings:
   124→        log(f"         boilerplate duplication: {len(findings)} clusters")
   125→    distinct_files = len({loc["file"] for e in entries for loc in e["locations"]})
   126→    return findings, {"boilerplate_duplication": distinct_files}
   127→
   128→
   129→def _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries: list[dict], zone_map) -> list[dict]:
   130→    """Keep only in-scope, zone-allowed boilerplate clusters.
   131→
   132→    jscpd can return files that are outside language discovery (artifacts/docs).
   133→    Restricting to known zone-map files prevents unknown paths from being treated
   134→    as production findings.
   135→    """
   136→    if zone_map is None:
   137→        return entries
   138→
   139→    known_files = set(zone_map.all_files())
   140→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   141→    skipped = 0
   142→    for entry in entries:
   143→        locations = entry.get("locations", [])
   144→        kept_locations = [
   145→            loc
   146→            for loc in locations
   147→            if loc.get("file") in known_files
   148→            and not should_skip_finding(
   149→                zone_map,
   150→                loc.get("file", ""),
   151→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   152→            )
   153→        ]
   154→        distinct_files = {loc["file"] for loc in kept_locations}
   155→        if len(distinct_files) < 2:
   156→            skipped += 1
   157→            continue
   158→
   159→        normalized = dict(entry)
   160→        normalized["locations"] = sorted(
   161→            kept_locations,
   162→            key=lambda item: (item.get("file", ""), item.get("line", 0)),
   163→        )
   164→        normalized["distinct_files"] = len(distinct_files)
   165→        filtered.append(normalized)
   166→
   167→    if skipped:
   168→        log(f"         zones: {skipped} boilerplate clusters excluded")
   169→    return filtered
   170→

   172→def find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> set[str]:
   173→    """Find test files in standard locations outside the scanned path."""
   174→    extra = set()
   175→    path_root = path.resolve()
   176→    project_root = get_project_root()
   177→    test_dirs = lang.external_test_dirs or ["tests", "test"]
   178→    exts = tuple(lang.test_file_extensions or lang.extensions)
   179→    for test_dir in test_dirs:
   180→        d = project_root / test_dir
   181→        if not d.is_dir():
   182→            continue
   183→        if d.resolve().is_relative_to(path_root):
   184→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it
   185→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   186→            for filename in files:
   187→                if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in exts):
   188→                    extra.add(os.path.join(root, filename))
   189→    return extra
   190→
   191→
   192→def _entries_to_findings(
   193→    detector: str,
   194→    entries: list[dict],
   195→    *,
   196→    default_name: str = "",
   197→    include_zone: bool = False,
   198→    zone_map=None,
   199→) -> list[Finding]:
   200→    """Convert detector entries to normalized findings."""
   201→    results: list[Finding] = []
   202→    for entry in entries:
   203→        finding = make_finding(
   204→            detector,
   205→            entry["file"],
   206→            entry.get("name", default_name),
   207→            tier=entry["tier"],
   208→            confidence=entry["confidence"],
   209→            summary=entry["summary"],
   210→            detail=entry.get("detail", {}),
   211→        )
   212→        if include_zone and zone_map is not None:
   213→            z = zone_map.get(entry["file"])
   214→            if z is not None:
   215→                finding["zone"] = z.value
   216→        results.append(finding)
   217→    return results
   218→

   220→def _log_phase_summary(label: str, results: list[Finding], potential: int, unit: str) -> None:
   221→    """Emit standardized shared-phase summary logging."""
   222→    if results:
   223→        log(f"         {label}: {len(results)} findings ({potential} {unit})")
   224→    else:
   225→        log(f"         {label}: clean ({potential} {unit})")

   227→
   228→def _coverage_to_dict(coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus) -> dict[str, object]:
   229→    return {
   230→        "detector": coverage.detector,
   231→        "status": coverage.status,
   232→        "confidence": round(coerce_confidence(coverage.confidence), 2),
   233→        "summary": coverage.summary,
   234→        "impact": coverage.impact,
   235→        "remediation": coverage.remediation,
   236→        "tool": coverage.tool,
   237→        "reason": coverage.reason,
   238→    }
   239→
   240→
   241→def _merge_detector_coverage(
   242→    existing: dict[str, object],
   243→    incoming: dict[str, object],
   244→) -> dict[str, object]:
   245→    merged = dict(existing)
   246→    merged["status"] = (
   247→        "reduced"
   248→        if str(existing.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   249→        or str(incoming.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   250→        else "full"
   251→    )
   252→    merged["confidence"] = round(
   253→        min(
   254→            coerce_confidence(existing.get("confidence")),
   255→            coerce_confidence(incoming.get("confidence")),
   256→        ),
   257→        2,
   258→    )
   259→
   260→    for key in ("summary", "impact", "remediation", "tool", "reason"):
   261→        current = str(merged.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   262→        update = str(incoming.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   263→        if update and not current:
   264→            merged[key] = update
   265→        elif update and current and update not in current:
   266→            merged[key] = f"{current} | {update}"
   267→    return merged
   268→
   269→
   270→def _record_detector_coverage(lang: LangRuntimeContract, coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus | None) -> None:
   271→    if coverage is None:
   272→        return
   273→    normalized = _coverage_to_dict(coverage)
   274→    detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   275→    if not detector:
   276→        return
   277→    existing = lang.detector_coverage.get(detector)
   278→    if isinstance(existing, dict):
   279→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = _merge_detector_coverage(existing, normalized)
   280→    else:
   281→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = normalized
   282→
   283→
   284→def phase_security(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   285→    """Shared phase: detect security issues (cross-language + lang-specific)."""
   286→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   287→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   288→    entries, cross_lang_scanned = detect_security_issues(
   289→        files,
   290→        zone_map,
   291→        lang.name,
   292→        scan_root=path,
   293→    )
   294→    lang_scanned = 0
   295→
   296→    # Also call lang-specific security detectors.
   297→    lang_result = lang.detect_lang_security_detailed(files, zone_map)
   298→    if isinstance(lang_result, LangSecurityResult):
   299→        lang_entries = lang_result.entries
   300→        lang_scanned = max(0, int(lang_result.files_scanned))
   301→        _record_detector_coverage(lang, lang_result.coverage)
   302→    else:
   303→        # Backwards compatibility for legacy plugins returning tuple[list[dict], int].
   304→        lang_entries, legacy_scanned = lang_result
   305→        lang_scanned = max(0, int(legacy_scanned or 0))
   306→    entries.extend(lang_entries)
   307→
   308→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "security")
   309→    potential = max(cross_lang_scanned, lang_scanned)
   310→
   311→    results = _entries_to_findings(
   312→        "security",
   313→        entries,
   314→        include_zone=True,
   315→        zone_map=zone_map,
   316→    )
   317→    _log_phase_summary("security", results, potential, "files scanned")
   318→
   319→    if "security" not in lang.detector_coverage:
   320→        lang.detector_coverage["security"] = {
   321→            "detector": "security",
   322→            "status": "full",
   323→            "confidence": 1.0,
   324→            "summary": "Security coverage complete for enabled detectors.",
   325→            "impact": "",
   326→            "remediation": "",
   327→            "tool": "",
   328→            "reason": "",
   329→        }
   330→
   331→    return results, {"security": potential}

   377→def phase_subjective_review(
   378→    path: Path,
   379→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   380→) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   381→    """Shared phase: detect files missing subjective design review."""
   382→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   383→    max_age = lang.review_max_age_days
   384→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   385→    review_cache = lang.review_cache
   386→    if isinstance(review_cache, dict) and "files" in review_cache:
   387→        per_file_cache = review_cache.get("files", {})
   388→    else:
   389→        # Legacy format: flat dict of file entries with no "files" wrapper.
   390→        # Filter out known top-level structural keys so they aren't treated as
   391→        # file paths, then reconstruct the canonical shape preserving them.
   392→        _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset({"holistic"})
   393→        raw = review_cache if isinstance(review_cache, dict) else {}
   394→        per_file_cache = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k not in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}
   395→        review_cache = {"files": per_file_cache}
   396→        if "holistic" in raw:
   397→            review_cache["holistic"] = raw["holistic"]
   398→
   399→    entries, potential = detect_review_coverage(
   400→        files,
   401→        zone_map,
   402→        per_file_cache,
   403→        lang.name,
   404→        low_value_pattern=lang.review_low_value_pattern,
   405→        max_age_days=max_age,
   406→        holistic_cache=review_cache.get("holistic")
   407→        if isinstance(review_cache, dict)
   408→        else None,
   409→        holistic_total_files=len(files),
   410→    )
   411→
   412→    # Also check holistic review staleness.
   413→    holistic_entries = detect_holistic_review_staleness(
   414→        review_cache,
   415→        total_files=len(files),
   416→        max_age_days=max_age,
   417→    )
   418→    entries.extend(holistic_entries)
   419→
   420→    results = _entries_to_findings("subjective_review", entries)
   421→    _log_phase_summary("subjective review", results, potential, "reviewable files")
   422→
   423→    return results, {"subjective_review": potential}
   424→

   426→def phase_signature(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   427→    """Shared phase runner: detect signature variance via lang.extract_functions.
   428→
   429→    Backend-agnostic — works with any extractor that returns FunctionInfo objects
   430→    (tree-sitter, regex, AST, etc.).  Returns empty results when the lang has no
   431→    function extractor.
   432→    """
   433→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   434→
   435→    findings: list[Finding] = []
   436→    potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
   437→
   438→    if not functions:
   439→        return findings, potentials
   440→
   441→    entries, _total = detect_signature_variance(functions, min_occurrences=3)
   442→    for e in entries:
   443→        findings.append(make_finding(
   444→            "signature", e["files"][0],
   445→            f"signature_variance::{e['name']}",
   446→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   447→            summary=(
   448→                f"'{e['name']}' has {e['signature_count']} different signatures "
   449→                f"across {e['file_count']} files"
   450→            ),
   451→        ))
   452→    if entries:
   453→        potentials["signature"] = len(entries)
   454→        log(f"         signature variance: {len(entries)}")
   455→
   456→    return findings, potentials

   458→
   459→def run_structural_phase(
   460→    path: Path,
   461→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   462→    *,
   463→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   464→    log_fn,
   465→    min_loc: int = 40,
   466→    god_rules=None,
   467→    god_extractor_fn=None,
   468→    extra_signal_entries_fn: Callable[
   469→        [Path, LangRuntimeContract], list[dict[str, object]]
   470→    ]
   471→    | None = None,
   472→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   473→    """Run large/complexity/flat directory detectors for a language.
   474→
   475→    Optional ``god_rules`` + ``god_extractor_fn`` enable god-class detection:
   476→    when both are provided, ``god_extractor_fn(path)`` is called to extract
   477→    class info, then ``detect_gods()`` finds classes matching multiple rules.
   478→    ``extra_signal_entries_fn`` allows language-specific structural signals to
   479→    merge through the same structural pipeline contract.
   480→    """
   481→    structural: dict[str, dict] = {}
   482→
   483→    large_entries, file_count = large_detector_mod.detect_large_files(
   484→        path,
   485→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   486→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   487→    )
   488→    for entry in large_entries:
   489→        add_structural_signal(
   490→            structural,
   491→            entry["file"],
   492→            f"large ({entry['loc']} LOC)",
   493→            {"loc": entry["loc"]},
   494→        )
   495→
   496→    try:
   497→        complexity_entries, _ = complexity_detector_mod.detect_complexity(
   498→            path,
   499→            signals=complexity_signals,
   500→            file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   501→            threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   502→            min_loc=min_loc,
   503→        )
   504→    except TypeError:
   505→        # Backward-compatible fallback for tests/plugins monkeypatching the
   506→        # detector with the pre-min_loc callable shape.
   507→        complexity_entries, _ = complexity_detector_mod.detect_complexity(
   508→            path,
   509→            signals=complexity_signals,
   510→            file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   511→            threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   512→        )
   513→    for entry in complexity_entries:
   514→        add_structural_signal(
   515→            structural,
   516→            entry["file"],
   517→            f"complexity score {entry['score']}",
   518→            {"complexity_score": entry["score"], "complexity_signals": entry["signals"]},
   519→        )
   520→        lang.complexity_map[entry["file"]] = entry["score"]
   521→
   522→    if god_rules and god_extractor_fn:
   523→        god_entries, _ = detect_gods(god_extractor_fn(path), god_rules, min_reasons=2)
   524→        for entry in god_entries:
   525→            add_structural_signal(
   526→                structural, entry["file"], entry["signal_text"], entry["detail"],
   527→            )
   528→        if god_entries:
   529→            log_fn(f"         god classes: {len(god_entries)}")
   530→
   531→    if extra_signal_entries_fn is not None:
   532→        extra_entries = extra_signal_entries_fn(path, lang)
   533→        for entry in extra_entries:
   534→            file_value = str(entry.get("file", "")).strip()
   535→            signal_text = str(entry.get("signal_text", "")).strip()
   536→            detail = entry.get("detail")
   537→            if not file_value or not signal_text:
   538→                continue
   539→            add_structural_signal(
   540→                structural,
   541→                file_value,
   542→                signal_text,
   543→                detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {},
   544→            )
   545→
   546→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log_fn)
   547→    flat_entries, analyzed_dir_count = flat_dirs_detector_mod.detect_flat_dirs(
   548→        path, file_finder=lang.file_finder
   549→    )
   550→    for entry in flat_entries:
   551→        child_dir_count = int(entry.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   552→        combined_score = int(entry.get("combined_score", entry.get("file_count", 0)))
   553→        results.append(
   554→            make_finding(
   555→                "flat_dirs",
   556→                entry["directory"],
   557→                "",
   558→                tier=3,
   559→                confidence="medium",
   560→                summary=flat_dirs_detector_mod.format_flat_dir_summary(entry),
   561→                detail={
   562→                    "file_count": entry["file_count"],
   563→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   564→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   565→                    "kind": entry.get("kind", "overload"),
   566→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   567→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(entry.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   568→                    "sparse_child_count": int(entry.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   569→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(entry.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   570→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   571→                        entry.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   572→                    ),
   573→                },
   574→            )
   575→        )
   576→    if flat_entries:
   577→        log_fn(
   578→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   579→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   580→        )
   581→
   582→    potentials = {
   583→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   584→        "flat_dirs": analyzed_dir_count,
   585→    }
   586→    return results, potentials
   587→
   588→
   589→def run_coupling_phase(
   590→    path: Path,
   591→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   592→    *,
   593→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   594→    log_fn,
   595→    post_process_fn=None,
   596→    single_use_skip_dir_names: set[str] | None = None,
   597→    orphaned_options: OrphanedDetectionOptions | None = None,
   598→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   599→    """Run single-use/cycles/orphaned detectors against a language dep graph.
   600→
   601→    Optional ``post_process_fn(findings, entries, lang)`` is called after
   602→    creating single-use and orphaned findings to allow per-language
   603→    adjustments (e.g. confidence gating based on corroboration signals).
   604→    Optional ``single_use_skip_dir_names`` and ``orphaned_options`` allow
   605→    language-specific orchestration without re-implementing phase flow.
   606→    """
   607→    graph = build_dep_graph_fn(path)
   608→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   609→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   610→    results: list[dict] = []
   611→
   612→    single_entries, single_candidates = (
   613→        single_use_detector_mod.detect_single_use_abstractions(
   614→        path,
   615→        graph,
   616→        barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   617→        )
   618→    )
   619→    single_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, single_entries, "single_use")
   620→    single_findings = make_single_use_findings(
   621→        single_entries,
   622→        lang.get_area,
   623→        skip_dir_names=single_use_skip_dir_names,
   624→        stderr_fn=log_fn,
   625→    )
   626→    if post_process_fn:
   627→        post_process_fn(single_findings, single_entries, lang)
   628→    results.extend(single_findings)
   629→
   630→    cycle_entries, _ = graph_detector_mod.detect_cycles(graph)
   631→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   632→    results.extend(make_cycle_findings(cycle_entries, log_fn))
   633→
   634→    resolved_orphaned_options = orphaned_options or OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   635→        extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   636→        extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   637→    )
   638→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = orphaned_detector_mod.detect_orphaned_files(
   639→        path,
   640→        graph,
   641→        extensions=list(lang.extensions),
   642→        options=resolved_orphaned_options,
   643→    )
   644→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   645→    orphan_findings = make_orphaned_findings(orphan_entries, log_fn)
   646→    if post_process_fn:
   647→        post_process_fn(orphan_findings, orphan_entries, lang)
   648→    results.extend(orphan_findings)
   649→
   650→    log_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} coupling/structural findings total")
   651→    potentials = {
   652→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zone_map, single_candidates),
   653→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   654→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   655→    }
   656→    return results, potentials
   657→
   658→
   659→def make_structural_coupling_phase_pair(
   660→    *,
   661→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   662→    build_dep_graph_fn: Callable[[Path], dict[str, dict[str, object]]],
   663→    log_fn: Callable[[str], None],
   664→) -> tuple[
   665→    Callable[[Path, LangRuntimeContract], tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]],
   666→    Callable[[Path, LangRuntimeContract], tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]],
   667→]:
   668→    """Create default structural/coupling phase callables for a language.
   669→
   670→    This keeps language phase modules declarative by letting them provide only
   671→    their complexity signals and dependency-graph builder.
   672→    """
   673→
   674→    def phase_structural(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   675→        return run_structural_phase(
   676→            path,
   677→            lang,
   678→            complexity_signals=complexity_signals,
   679→            log_fn=log_fn,
   680→        )
   681→
   682→    def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   683→        return run_coupling_phase(
   684→            path,
   685→            lang,
   686→            build_dep_graph_fn=build_dep_graph_fn,
   687→            log_fn=log_fn,
   688→        )
   689→
   690→    return phase_structural, phase_coupling
   691→
   692→
   693→__all__ = [
   694→    "find_external_test_files",
   695→    "make_structural_coupling_phase_pair",
   696→    "phase_boilerplate_duplication",
   697→    "phase_dupes",
   698→    "phase_private_imports",
   699→    "phase_security",
   700→    "phase_signature",
   701→    "phase_subjective_review",
   702→    "phase_test_coverage",
   703→    "run_coupling_phase",
   704→    "run_structural_phase",
   705→]
   706→

    30→    name_no_ext = str(Path(r).with_suffix(""))
    31→
    32→    for target in dynamic_targets:
    33→        resolved = alias_resolver(target) if alias_resolver else target
    34→        resolved = resolved.lstrip("./")
    35→        if resolved == name_no_ext or resolved == r:
    36→            return True
    37→        if name_no_ext.endswith("/" + resolved) or name_no_ext.endswith(resolved):
    38→            return True
    39→        if resolved.endswith("/" + stem) or resolved == stem:
    40→            return True
    41→        if resolved.endswith("/" + Path(filepath).name):
    42→            return True
    43→
    44→    return False
    45→
    46→
    47→def _orphan_skip_reason(
    48→    *,
    49→    filepath: str,
    50→    entry: dict,
    51→    entry_patterns: list[str],
    52→    barrel_names: set[str],
    53→    dynamic_targets: set[str],
    54→    alias_resolver: Callable[[str], str] | None,
    55→) -> str | None:
    56→    """Return skip reason for a candidate file, or None when it should be checked."""
    57→    if entry["importer_count"] > 0:
    58→        return "has_importers"
    59→    rel_path = rel(filepath)
    60→    if any(pattern in rel_path for pattern in entry_patterns):
    61→        return "entry_pattern"
    62→    if Path(filepath).name in barrel_names:
    63→        return "barrel"
    64→    if dynamic_targets and _is_dynamically_imported(
    65→        filepath,
    66→        dynamic_targets,
    67→        alias_resolver,
    68→    ):
    69→        return "dynamic_import"
    70→    return None
    71→
    72→
    73→def _file_loc(filepath: str) -> int:
    74→    """Return file LOC (0 when unreadable)."""
    75→    try:
    76→        return len(Path(filepath).read_text().splitlines())
    77→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    78→        return 0
    79→
    80→
    81→def detect_orphaned_files(
    82→    path: Path,
    83→    graph: dict,
    84→    extensions: list[str],
    85→    options: OrphanedDetectionOptions | None = None,
    86→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    87→    """Find files with zero importers that aren't known entry points."""
    88→    resolved_options = options or OrphanedDetectionOptions()
    89→    all_entry_patterns = resolved_options.extra_entry_patterns or []
    90→    all_barrel_names = resolved_options.extra_barrel_names or set()
    91→    dynamic_import_finder = resolved_options.dynamic_import_finder
    92→    alias_resolver = resolved_options.alias_resolver
    93→
    94→    dynamic_targets = (
    95→        dynamic_import_finder(path, extensions) if dynamic_import_finder else set()
    96→    )
    97→
    98→    total_files = len(graph)
    99→    entries = []
   100→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
   101→        skip_reason = _orphan_skip_reason(
   102→            filepath=filepath,
   103→            entry=entry,
   104→            entry_patterns=all_entry_patterns,
   105→            barrel_names=all_barrel_names,
   106→            dynamic_targets=dynamic_targets,
   107→            alias_resolver=alias_resolver,
   108→        )
   109→        if skip_reason is not None:
   110→            continue
   111→
   112→        loc = _file_loc(filepath)
   113→        if loc < 10:
   114→            continue
   115→
   116→        entries.append(
   117→            {
   118→                "file": filepath,
   119→                "loc": loc,
   120→                "import_count": entry.get("import_count", 0),
   121→            }
   122→        )
   123→
   124→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), total_files
   125→

    29→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    30→class SkipItemsOptions:
    31→    """Options for skip-item queue operations."""
    32→

    34→    reason: str | None = None

    41→def _resolve_skip_item_options(
    42→    *,
    43→    options: SkipItemsOptions | None = None,
    44→    **legacy_options: Any,
    45→) -> SkipItemsOptions:
    46→    """Normalize skip option aliases while preserving legacy kwargs."""
    47→    if options is not None:
    48→        if legacy_options:
    49→            unexpected = ", ".join(sorted(legacy_options))
    50→            raise TypeError(
    51→                f"skip_items() got legacy kwargs with options=: {unexpected}"
    52→            )
    53→        return options

    55→    values: dict[str, Any] = {
    56→        "kind": "temporary",
    57→        "reason": None,
    58→        "note": None,
    59→        "attestation": None,
    60→        "review_after": None,
    61→        "scan_count": 0,
    62→    }
    63→    for key, value in legacy_options.items():
    64→        if key not in _SKIP_ITEM_OPTION_KEYS:
    65→            raise TypeError(f"skip_items() got an unexpected keyword argument '{key}'")
    66→        values[key] = value
    67→    return SkipItemsOptions(
    68→        kind=str(values["kind"] or "temporary"),
    69→        reason=values["reason"] if isinstance(values["reason"], str) else values["reason"],
    70→        note=values["note"] if isinstance(values["note"], str) else values["note"],
    71→        attestation=(
    72→            values["attestation"]
    73→            if isinstance(values["attestation"], str)
    74→            else values["attestation"]
    75→        ),
    76→        review_after=(
    77→            values["review_after"]
    78→            if isinstance(values["review_after"], int) or values["review_after"] is None

    89→def _remove_id_from_lists(plan: PlanModel, finding_id: str) -> None:
    90→    """Remove a finding ID from queue_order and skipped."""
    91→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
    92→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
    93→    if finding_id in order:
    94→        order.remove(finding_id)
    95→    skipped.pop(finding_id, None)
    96→

    98→def _resolve_position(
    99→    order: list[str],
   100→    position: str,
   101→    target: str | None = None,
   102→    offset: int | None = None,
   103→    finding_ids: list[str] | None = None,
   104→) -> int:
   105→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
   106→
   107→    *finding_ids* are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
   108→    positions when they already exist in the list.
   109→    """
   110→    moving = set(finding_ids or [])
   111→
   112→    boundary_idx = _resolve_boundary_position(order, position)
   113→    if boundary_idx is not None:
   114→        return boundary_idx
   115→
   116→    target_idx = _resolve_target_position(order, position, target, moving)
   117→    if target_idx is not None:
   118→        return target_idx
   119→
   120→    shifted_idx = _resolve_shift_position(order, position, offset, finding_ids, moving)
   121→    if shifted_idx is not None:
   122→        return shifted_idx
   123→
   124→    return len(order)
   125→
   126→
   127→def _resolve_boundary_position(order: list[str], position: str) -> int | None:
   128→    if position == "top":
   129→        return 0
   130→    if position == "bottom":
   131→        return len(order)
   132→    return None
   133→
   134→
   135→def _resolve_target_position(
   136→    order: list[str],
   137→    position: str,
   138→    target: str | None,
   139→    moving: set[str],
   140→) -> int | None:
   141→    if position == "before" and target:
   142→        for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
   143→            if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
   144→                return i
   145→        return 0
   146→    if position == "after" and target:
   147→        for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
   148→            if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
   149→                return i + 1
   150→        return len(order)
   151→    return None
   152→
   153→
   154→def _resolve_shift_position(
   155→    order: list[str],
   156→    position: str,
   157→    offset: int | None,
   158→    finding_ids: list[str] | None,
   159→    moving: set[str],
   160→) -> int | None:
   161→    if position not in {"up", "down"} or offset is None:
   162→        return None
   163→
   164→    if not finding_ids:
   165→        return 0 if position == "up" else len(order)
   166→
   167→    clean_order = [item_id for item_id in order if item_id not in moving]
   168→    current_idx_clean = _clean_index_for_first_id(order, finding_ids[0], moving)
   169→
   170→    if current_idx_clean is None:
   171→        if position == "up":
   172→            # Preserve existing behavior for unknown members.
   173→            return max(0, len(clean_order) - offset)
   174→        return len(clean_order)
   175→
   176→    if position == "up":
   177→        return max(0, current_idx_clean - offset)
   178→    return min(len(clean_order), current_idx_clean + offset)
   179→
   180→
   181→def _clean_index_for_first_id(
   182→    order: list[str],
   183→    first_id: str,
   184→    moving: set[str],
   185→) -> int | None:
   186→    non_moving_seen = 0
   187→    for item_id in order:
   188→        if item_id == first_id:
   189→            return non_moving_seen
   190→        if item_id not in moving:
   191→            non_moving_seen += 1
   192→    return None

   198→
   199→def move_items(
   200→    plan: PlanModel,
   201→    finding_ids: list[str],
   202→    position: str,
   203→    target: str | None = None,
   204→    offset: int | None = None,
   205→) -> int:
   206→    """Move finding IDs to a position in queue_order. Returns count moved."""
   207→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   208→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   209→
   210→    # Remove from skipped if present
   211→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
   212→    for fid in finding_ids:
   213→        skipped.pop(fid, None)
   214→
   215→    # Remove from current position in order
   216→    for fid in finding_ids:
   217→        if fid in order:
   218→            order.remove(fid)
   219→
   220→    # Resolve insertion point
   221→    idx = _resolve_position(order, position, target, offset, finding_ids)
   222→
   223→    # Insert in original order
   224→    for i, fid in enumerate(finding_ids):
   225→        order.insert(idx + i, fid)
   226→
   227→    return len(finding_ids)

   234→def skip_items(
   235→    plan: PlanModel,
   236→    finding_ids: list[str],
   237→    *,
   238→    options: SkipItemsOptions | None = None,
   239→    **legacy_options: Any,

   241→    """Move finding IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""
   242→    skip_options = _resolve_skip_item_options(
   243→        options=options,
   244→        **legacy_options,
   245→    )
   246→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   247→    now = utc_now()
   248→    count = 0
   249→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   250→    for fid in finding_ids:
   251→        _remove_id_from_lists(plan, fid)
   252→        skipped[fid] = {
   253→            "finding_id": fid,
   254→            "kind": skip_options.kind,
   255→            "reason": skip_options.reason,
   256→            "note": skip_options.note,
   257→            "attestation": skip_options.attestation,
   258→            "created_at": now,
   259→            "review_after": skip_options.review_after,
   260→            "skipped_at_scan": skip_options.scan_count,
   261→        }
   262→        count += 1
   263→    return count
   264→
   265→
   266→def unskip_items(
   267→    plan: PlanModel, finding_ids: list[str]
   268→) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
   269→    """Bring finding IDs back from skipped to the end of queue_order.
   270→
   271→    Returns ``(count_unskipped, permanent_ids_needing_state_reopen)``
   272→    where the second list contains IDs that were permanent or false_positive
   273→    and need their state-layer status reopened by the caller.
   274→    """
   275→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   276→    count = 0
   277→    need_reopen: list[str] = []
   278→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   279→    for fid in finding_ids:
   280→        entry = skipped.pop(fid, None)
   281→        if entry is not None:
   282→            if entry.get("kind") in ("permanent", "false_positive"):
   283→                need_reopen.append(fid)
   284→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   285→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   286→            count += 1
   287→    return count, need_reopen

   290→def resurface_stale_skips(
   291→    plan: PlanModel, current_scan_count: int
   292→) -> list[str]:
   293→    """Move temporary skips past their review_after threshold back to queue.
   294→
   295→    Returns list of resurfaced finding IDs.
   296→    """
   297→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   298→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   299→    resurfaced: list[str] = []
   300→    for fid in list(skipped):
   301→        entry = skipped[fid]
   302→        if entry.get("kind") != "temporary":
   303→            continue
   304→        review_after = entry.get("review_after")
   305→        if review_after is None:
   306→            continue
   307→        skipped_at = entry.get("skipped_at_scan", 0)
   308→        if current_scan_count >= skipped_at + review_after:
   309→            skipped.pop(fid)
   310→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   311→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   312→            resurfaced.append(fid)
   313→    return resurfaced

   350→def create_cluster(
   351→    plan: PlanModel,
   352→    name: str,
   353→    description: str | None = None,
   354→    action: str | None = None,
   355→) -> Cluster:
   356→    """Create a named cluster. Raises ValueError if it already exists."""
   357→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   358→    if name.startswith("auto/"):
   359→        raise ValueError(
   360→            f"Cluster names starting with 'auto/' are reserved for auto-clusters: {name!r}"
   361→        )
   362→    if name in plan["clusters"]:
   363→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {name!r} already exists")
   364→    now = utc_now()
   365→    cluster: Cluster = {
   366→        "name": name,
   367→        "description": description,
   368→        "finding_ids": [],
   369→        "created_at": now,
   370→        "updated_at": now,
   371→        "auto": False,
   372→        "cluster_key": "",
   373→        "action": action,
   374→        "user_modified": False,
   375→    }
   376→    plan["clusters"][name] = cluster

   380→def add_to_cluster(
   381→    plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str, finding_ids: list[str]
   382→) -> int:
   383→    """Add finding IDs to a cluster. Returns count added."""
   384→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   385→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
   386→    if cluster is None:
   387→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   388→
   389→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["finding_ids"]
   390→    count = 0
   391→    now = utc_now()
   392→    for fid in finding_ids:
   393→        if fid not in member_ids:
   394→            member_ids.append(fid)
   395→            count += 1
   396→        # Update override to track cluster membership
   397→        overrides = plan["overrides"]
   398→        if fid not in overrides:
   399→            overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   400→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = cluster_name
   401→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   402→
   403→    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   404→    return count

   407→def remove_from_cluster(
   408→    plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str, finding_ids: list[str]
   409→) -> int:
   410→    """Remove finding IDs from a cluster. Returns count removed."""
   411→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   412→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
   413→    if cluster is None:
   414→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   415→
   416→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["finding_ids"]
   417→    now = utc_now()
   418→    count = 0
   419→    for fid in finding_ids:
   420→        if fid in member_ids:
   421→            member_ids.remove(fid)
   422→            count += 1
   423→        # Clear cluster from override
   424→        override = plan["overrides"].get(fid)
   425→        if override and override.get("cluster") == cluster_name:
   426→            override["cluster"] = None
   427→            override["updated_at"] = now
   428→
   429→    # Mark auto-clusters as user_modified when items are manually removed
   430→    if count > 0 and cluster.get("auto"):
   431→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   432→
   433→    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   434→    return count

   437→def delete_cluster(plan: PlanModel, name: str) -> list[str]:
   438→    """Delete a cluster and clear cluster refs from overrides. Returns orphaned IDs."""
   439→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   440→    cluster = plan["clusters"].pop(name, None)
   441→    if cluster is None:
   442→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {name!r} does not exist")
   443→
   444→    orphaned = list(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   445→    now = utc_now()
   446→    for fid in orphaned:
   447→        override = plan["overrides"].get(fid)
   448→        if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   449→            override["cluster"] = None
   450→            override["updated_at"] = now
   451→
   452→    if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   453→        plan["active_cluster"] = None
   454→
   455→    return orphaned

   458→def move_cluster(
   459→    plan: PlanModel,
   460→    cluster_name: str,
   461→    position: str,
   462→    target: str | None = None,
   463→    offset: int | None = None,
   464→) -> int:
   465→    """Move all cluster members as a contiguous block. Returns count moved."""
   466→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   467→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
   468→    if cluster is None:
   469→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   470→
   471→    member_ids = list(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   472→    if not member_ids:
   473→        return 0
   474→
   475→    return move_items(plan, member_ids, position, target, offset)

   500→def reset_plan(plan: PlanModel) -> None:
   501→    """Reset plan to empty state, preserving version and created timestamp."""
   502→    created = plan.get("created", utc_now())

   509→def purge_ids(plan: PlanModel, finding_ids: list[str]) -> int:
   510→    """Remove finding IDs from the plan entirely.
   511→
   512→    Cleans queue_order, skipped, and all cluster memberships.
   513→    Does NOT touch overrides (descriptions/notes are kept for history).
   514→    Returns count of IDs that were actually present somewhere.
   515→    """
   516→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   517→    found = 0
   518→
   519→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   520→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   521→    for fid in finding_ids:
   522→        was_present = False
   523→        if fid in order:
   524→            order.remove(fid)
   525→            was_present = True
   526→        if fid in skipped:
   527→            skipped.pop(fid)
   528→            was_present = True
   529→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   530→            ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   531→            if fid in ids:
   532→                ids.remove(fid)
   533→                was_present = True
   534→        if was_present:
   535→            found += 1
   536→
   537→    return found
   538→

   238→def _ensure_state_containers(state: StateModel | dict) -> None:
   239→    """Ensure state top-level container fields are present and correctly typed."""
   240→    for key, value in empty_state().items():

   244→    if not isinstance(state.get("stats"), dict):

   256→def _normalize_finding_defaults(
   257→    *,
   258→    finding_id: str,
   259→    finding: dict,
   260→    state_created: str | None,
   261→) -> None:
   262→    """Apply default fields and normalization to one finding payload."""
   263→    finding.setdefault("id", finding_id)
   264→    finding.setdefault("detector", "unknown")
   265→    finding.setdefault("file", "")
   266→    finding.setdefault("tier", 3)
   267→    finding.setdefault("confidence", "low")
   268→    finding.setdefault("summary", "")
   269→    finding.setdefault("detail", {})
   270→    finding.setdefault("status", "open")
   271→    finding["status"] = canonical_finding_status(
   272→        finding.get("status"),
   273→        default="open",
   274→    )
   275→    finding.setdefault("note", None)
   276→    finding.setdefault("first_seen", state_created or utc_now())
   277→    finding.setdefault("last_seen", finding["first_seen"])
   278→    finding.setdefault("resolved_at", None)
   279→    finding["reopen_count"] = _as_non_negative_int(
   280→        finding.get("reopen_count", 0),
   281→        default=0,
   282→    )
   283→    finding.setdefault("suppressed", False)
   284→    finding.setdefault("suppressed_at", None)
   285→    finding.setdefault("suppression_pattern", None)

   288→def _normalize_findings(state: StateModel | dict) -> None:
   289→    """Normalize finding records and remove non-dict entries."""
   290→    findings = state["findings"]
   291→    to_remove = [
   292→        finding_id
   293→        for finding_id, finding in findings.items()
   294→        if not isinstance(finding, dict)
   295→    ]
   296→    for finding_id in to_remove:
   297→        findings.pop(finding_id, None)
   298→    state_created = state.get("created")
   299→    for finding_id, finding in findings.items():
   300→        _normalize_finding_defaults(
   301→            finding_id=finding_id,
   302→            finding=finding,
   303→            state_created=state_created,
   304→        )

   308→    """Normalize subjective integrity payload shape in scan history entries."""
   309→    for entry in state["scan_history"]:
   310→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   311→            continue
   312→        integrity = entry.get("subjective_integrity")
   313→        if integrity is not None and not isinstance(integrity, dict):

   317→def ensure_state_defaults(state: StateModel | dict) -> None:
   318→    """Normalize loose/legacy state payloads to a valid base shape in-place."""
   319→    _ensure_state_containers(state)
   320→    _normalize_findings(state)
   321→    _normalize_scan_history_entries(state)

   326→def validate_state_invariants(state: StateModel) -> None:
   327→    """Raise ValueError when core state invariants are violated."""
   328→    if not isinstance(state.get("findings"), dict):
   329→        raise ValueError("state.findings must be a dict")
   330→    if not isinstance(state.get("stats"), dict):
   331→        raise ValueError("state.stats must be a dict")
   332→
   333→    findings = state["findings"]
   334→    for finding_id, finding in findings.items():
   335→        if not isinstance(finding, dict):
   336→            raise ValueError(f"finding {finding_id!r} must be a dict")
   337→        if finding.get("id") != finding_id:
   338→            raise ValueError(f"finding id mismatch for {finding_id!r}")
   339→        if finding.get("status") not in _ALLOWED_FINDING_STATUSES:
   340→            raise ValueError(
   341→                f"finding {finding_id!r} has invalid status {finding.get('status')!r}"
   342→            )
   343→
   344→        tier = finding.get("tier")
   345→        if not isinstance(tier, int) or tier < 1 or tier > 4:
   346→            raise ValueError(f"finding {finding_id!r} has invalid tier {tier!r}")
   347→
   348→        reopen_count = finding.get("reopen_count")
   349→        if not isinstance(reopen_count, int) or reopen_count < 0:
   350→            raise ValueError(
   351→                f"finding {finding_id!r} has invalid reopen_count {reopen_count!r}"
   352→            )
   353→
   354→
   355→def require_findings(state: StateModel | dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Finding]:
   356→    """Return ``state['findings']`` and fail fast when contract is violated."""
   357→    findings = state.get("findings")
   358→    if not isinstance(findings, dict):
   359→        raise ValueError("state.findings must be a dict")
   360→    return findings
   361→
   362→
   363→def require_subjective_assessments(
   364→    state: StateModel | dict[str, Any],
   365→) -> dict[str, SubjectiveAssessment]:
   366→    """Return ``state['subjective_assessments']`` with strict contract checks."""
   367→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
   368→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict):
   369→        raise ValueError("state.subjective_assessments must be a dict")
   370→    return assessments
   371→
   372→
   373→def require_scan_count(state: StateModel | dict[str, Any]) -> int:
   374→    """Return normalized ``state['scan_count']`` and fail on missing/invalid values."""
   375→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count")
   376→    if not isinstance(scan_count, int) or scan_count < 0:
   377→        raise ValueError("state.scan_count must be a non-negative integer")
   378→    return scan_count
   379→
   380→
   381→def json_default(obj: Any) -> Any:
   382→    """JSON serializer that handles known types and rejects unknowns."""
   383→    if isinstance(obj, set):
   384→        return sorted(obj)
   385→    if isinstance(obj, Path):
   386→        return str(obj).replace("\\", "/")
   387→    if hasattr(obj, "isoformat"):
   388→        return obj.isoformat()
   389→    raise TypeError(
   390→        f"Object of type {type(obj).__name__} is not JSON serializable: {obj!r}"
   391→    )
   392→
   393→
   394→def get_overall_score(state: StateModel) -> float | None:
   395→    """Canonical overall score (lenient, includes subjective dimensions)."""
   396→    return state.get("overall_score")
   397→
   398→
   399→def get_objective_score(state: StateModel) -> float | None:
   400→    """Canonical objective score (lenient, mechanical dimensions only)."""
   401→    return state.get("objective_score")
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_strict_score(state: StateModel) -> float | None:
   405→    """Canonical strict score (strict, includes subjective dimensions)."""
   406→    return state.get("strict_score")

   408→

   414→    """

1→"""Core shared runtime helpers.
     2→
     3→Import concrete helpers from submodules (for example ``core.query``) instead of
     4→re-exporting from this package root. Legacy top-level facades now live under
     5→``desloppify.compat``.
     6→
     7→Structured namespaces are available under:
     8→- ``desloppify.core.discovery`` (api/impl)
     9→- ``desloppify.core.pathing`` (api/impl)
    10→- ``desloppify.core.io`` (api/impl)
    11→"""
    12→
    13→from __future__ import annotations
    14→
    15→import importlib
    16→
    17→__all__ = ["discovery", "io", "pathing"]
    18→
    19→_LAZY_SUBMODULES = {
    20→    "discovery": "desloppify.core.discovery",
    21→    "io": "desloppify.core.io",
    22→    "pathing": "desloppify.core.pathing",
    23→}
    24→
    25→
    26→def __getattr__(name: str):
    27→    target = _LAZY_SUBMODULES.get(name)
    28→    if target is None:
    29→        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    30→    value = importlib.import_module(target)
    31→    globals()[name] = value
    32→    return value
    33→

   114→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value)))

   136→) -> None:

   151→
   152→    content = json.dumps(state, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n"
   153→

   162→                backup_ex,

   164→
   165→    try:

1→"""Helper utilities for work queue item construction."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→from fnmatch import fnmatch
     7→
     8→from desloppify.core.enums import finding_status_tokens
     9→from desloppify.core.registry import DETECTORS
    10→from desloppify.engine.planning.scorecard_projection import (
    11→    scorecard_subjective_entries,
    12→)
    13→from desloppify.intelligence.integrity import (
    14→    is_holistic_subjective_finding,
    15→    unassessed_subjective_dimensions,
    16→)
    17→from desloppify.scoring import DISPLAY_NAMES
    18→
    19→ALL_STATUSES = set(finding_status_tokens(include_all=True))
    20→ATTEST_EXAMPLE = (
    21→    "I have actually [DESCRIBE THE CONCRETE CHANGE YOU MADE] "
    22→    "and I am not gaming the score by resolving without fixing."
    23→)
    24→
    25→
    26→def detail_dict(item: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    27→    """Return finding detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    28→    detail = item.get("detail")
    29→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    30→
    31→
    32→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    33→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    34→
    35→
    36→def is_subjective_finding(item: dict) -> bool:
    37→    detector = item.get("detector")
    38→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    39→        return True
    40→    if detector == "holistic_review":
    41→        return True
    42→    return False
    43→
    44→
    45→def is_review_finding(item: dict) -> bool:
    46→    return item.get("detector") == "review"
    47→
    48→
    49→def review_finding_weight(item: dict) -> float:
    50→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    51→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    52→    weight_by_confidence = {
    53→        "high": 1.0,
    54→        "medium": 0.7,
    55→        "low": 0.3,
    56→    }
    57→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    58→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):
    59→        weight *= 10.0
    60→    return float(weight)
    61→
    62→
    63→def scope_matches(item: dict, scope: str | None) -> bool:
    64→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    65→    if not scope:
    66→        return True
    67→
    68→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    69→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    70→    filepath = item.get("file", "")
    71→    summary = item.get("summary", "")
    72→    dimension = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    73→    kind = item.get("kind", "")
    74→
    75→    if "*" in scope:
    76→        return any(
    77→            fnmatch(candidate, scope)
    78→            for candidate in (item_id, filepath, detector, dimension, summary)
    79→        )
    80→
    81→    if "::" in scope:
    82→        return item_id.startswith(scope)
    83→
    84→    lowered = scope.lower()
    85→    if kind == "subjective_dimension":
    86→        return (
    87→            lowered in item_id.lower()
    88→            or lowered in dimension.lower()
    89→            or lowered in summary.lower()
    90→        )
    91→
    92→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a finding ID.
    93→    if len(lowered) >= 8 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", lowered):
    94→        return item_id.lower().endswith("::" + lowered)
    95→
    96→    return (
    97→        detector == scope
    98→        or filepath == scope
    99→        or filepath.startswith(scope.rstrip("/") + "/")
   100→    )
   101→
   102→
   103→def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   104→    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]+", "_", text.lower()).strip("_")
   105→
   106→
   107→def _canonical_subjective_dimension_key(display_name: str) -> str:
   108→    """Map a display label (e.g. 'Mid elegance') to its canonical dimension key."""
   109→    cleaned = display_name.replace(" (subjective)", "").strip()
   110→    target = cleaned.lower()
   111→
   112→    for dim_key, label in DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   113→        if str(label).lower() == target:
   114→            return str(dim_key)
   115→    return slugify(cleaned)
   116→
   117→
   118→def _subjective_dimension_aliases(display_name: str) -> set[str]:
   119→    """Return normalized aliases used to match display labels with finding dimension keys."""
   120→    cleaned = display_name.replace(" (subjective)", "").strip()
   121→    canonical = _canonical_subjective_dimension_key(cleaned)
   122→    return {
   123→        cleaned.lower(),
   124→        cleaned.replace(" ", "_").lower(),
   125→        slugify(cleaned),
   126→        canonical.lower(),
   127→        slugify(canonical),
   128→    }
   129→
   130→
   131→def supported_fixers_for_item(state: dict, item: dict) -> set[str] | None:
   132→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   133→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()
   134→    if not lang:
   135→        return None
   136→
   137→    caps = state.get("lang_capabilities", {})
   138→    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
   139→        return None
   140→
   141→    lang_caps = caps.get(lang, {})
   142→    if not isinstance(lang_caps, dict):
   143→        return None
   144→
   145→    fixers = lang_caps.get("fixers")
   146→    if not isinstance(fixers, list):
   147→        return None
   148→    return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}
   149→
   150→
   151→def primary_command_for_finding(
   152→    item: dict, *, supported_fixers: set[str] | None = None
   153→) -> str:
   154→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
   155→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   156→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
   157→        available_fixers = [
   158→            fixer
   159→            for fixer in meta.fixers
   160→            if supported_fixers is None or fixer in supported_fixers
   161→        ]
   162→        if available_fixers:
   163→            return f"desloppify fix {available_fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   164→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   165→        if is_holistic_subjective_finding(item):
   166→            return "desloppify review --prepare"
   167→        return "desloppify show subjective"
   168→    return f'desloppify plan done "{item.get("id", "")}" --note "<what you did>" --attest "{ATTEST_EXAMPLE}"'
   169→
   170→
   171→def subjective_strict_scores(state: dict) -> dict[str, float]:
   172→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {}) or {}
   173→    if not dim_scores:
   174→        return {}
   175→
   176→    entries = scorecard_subjective_entries(state, dim_scores=dim_scores)
   177→    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   178→    for entry in entries:
   179→        name = str(entry.get("name", "")).strip()
   180→        if not name:
   181→            continue
   182→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
   183→        [REDACTED](name)
   184→        aliases = _subjective_dimension_aliases(name)
   185→        for cli_key in entry.get("cli_keys", []):
   186→            key = str(cli_key).strip().lower()
   187→            if not key:
   188→                continue
   189→            aliases.add(key)
   190→            aliases.add(slugify(key))
   191→        aliases.add(dim_key.lower())
   192→        aliases.add(slugify(dim_key))
   193→        for alias in aliases:
   194→            scores[alias] = strict_val
   195→    return scores
   196→
   197→
   198→def _normalized_subjective_threshold(threshold: float) -> float:
   199→    """Clamp subjective threshold to [0, 100]."""
   200→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, float(threshold)))
   201→
   202→
   203→def _open_review_findings_by_dimension(findings: dict) -> dict[str, int]:
   204→    """Count open review findings keyed by normalized dimension id."""
   205→    review_open_by_dim: dict[str, int] = {}
   206→    for finding in findings.values():
   207→        if finding.get("status") != "open" or finding.get("detector") != "review":
   208→            continue
   209→        dim_key = str(detail_dict(finding).get("dimension", "")).strip().lower()
   210→        if not dim_key:
   211→            continue
   212→        review_open_by_dim[dim_key] = review_open_by_dim.get(dim_key, 0) + 1
   213→    return review_open_by_dim
   214→
   215→
   216→def _entry_cli_keys(entry: dict) -> list[str]:
   217→    """Normalize CLI dimension keys from a scorecard entry."""
   218→    return [
   219→        str(key).strip().lower()
   220→        for key in entry.get("cli_keys", [])
   221→        if str(key).strip()
   222→    ]
   223→
   224→
   225→def _entry_aliases(name: str, cli_keys: list[str]) -> set[str]:
   226→    """Build all aliases used to join review findings for one subjective dimension."""
   227→    aliases = set(_subjective_dimension_aliases(name))
   228→    aliases.update(cli_keys)
   229→    aliases.update(slugify(key) for key in cli_keys)
   230→    return aliases
   231→
   232→
   233→def _is_unassessed_entry(
   234→    *,
   235→    entry: dict,
   236→    name: str,
   237→    strict_val: float,
   238→    unassessed_dims: set[str],
   239→) -> bool:
   240→    """Return whether a subjective entry should be treated as unassessed."""
   241→    return bool(entry.get("placeholder")) or (
   242→        name in unassessed_dims or (strict_val <= 0.0 and int(entry.get("issues", 0)) == 0)
   243→    )
   244→
   245→
   246→def _subjective_primary_command(
   247→    *,
   248→    is_unassessed: bool,
   249→    is_stale: bool,
   250→    open_review: int,
   251→    cli_keys: list[str],
   252→) -> str:
   253→    """Choose next command for a subjective queue item."""
   254→    if is_unassessed:
   255→        return "desloppify review --prepare"
   256→    if is_stale:
   257→        if cli_keys:
   258→            return "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions " + ",".join(cli_keys)
   259→        return "desloppify review --prepare"
   260→    if open_review > 0:
   261→        return "desloppify show review --status open"
   262→    if cli_keys:
   263→        return "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions " + ",".join(cli_keys)
   264→    return "desloppify review --prepare"
   265→
   266→
   267→def build_subjective_items(
   268→    state: dict, findings: dict, *, threshold: float = 100.0
   269→) -> list[dict]:
   270→    """Create synthetic subjective work items (always tier 4)."""
   271→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {}) or {}
   272→    if not dim_scores:
   273→        return []
   274→    threshold = _normalized_subjective_threshold(threshold)
   275→
   276→    subjective_entries = scorecard_subjective_entries(state, dim_scores=dim_scores)
   277→    if not subjective_entries:
   278→        return []
   279→    unassessed_dims = {
   280→        str(name).strip()
   281→        for name in unassessed_subjective_dimensions(
   282→            dim_scores
   283→        )
   284→    }
   285→
   286→    review_open_by_dim = _open_review_findings_by_dimension(findings)
   287→
   288→    items: list[dict] = []
   289→    for entry in subjective_entries:
   290→        name = str(entry.get("name", "")).strip()
   291→        if not name:
   292→            continue
   293→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
   294→        if strict_val >= threshold:
   295→            continue
   296→
   297→        [REDACTED](name)
   298→        cli_keys = _entry_cli_keys(entry)
   299→        aliases = _entry_aliases(name, cli_keys)
   300→        open_review = sum(review_open_by_dim.get(alias, 0) for alias in aliases)
   301→        is_unassessed = _is_unassessed_entry(
   302→            entry=entry,
   303→            name=name,
   304→            strict_val=strict_val,
   305→            unassessed_dims=unassessed_dims,
   306→        )
   307→        is_stale = bool(entry.get("stale"))
   308→        primary_command = _subjective_primary_command(
   309→            is_unassessed=is_unassessed,
   310→            is_stale=is_stale,
   311→            open_review=open_review,
   312→            cli_keys=cli_keys,
   313→        )
   314→        stale_tag = " [stale — re-review]" if is_stale else ""
   315→        summary = f"Subjective dimension below target: {name} ({strict_val:.1f}%){stale_tag}"
   316→        items.append(
   317→            {
   318→                "id": f"subjective::{slugify(dim_key)}",
   319→                "detector": "subjective_assessment",
   320→                "file": ".",
   321→                "tier": 4,
   322→                "effective_tier": 4,
   323→                "confidence": "medium",
   324→                "summary": summary,
   325→                "detail": {
   326→                    "dimension_name": name,
   327→                    "dimension": dim_key,
   328→                    "issues": int(entry.get("issues", 0)),
   329→                    "strict_score": strict_val,
   330→                    "open_review_findings": open_review,
   331→                    "cli_keys": cli_keys,
   332→                },
   333→                "status": "open",
   334→                "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   335→                "primary_command": primary_command,
   336→            }
   337→        )
   338→    return items
   339→
   340→
   341→__all__ = [
   342→    "ALL_STATUSES",
   343→    "ATTEST_EXAMPLE",

     2→
     3→Import concrete helpers from submodules (for example ``core.query``) instead of
     4→re-exporting from this package root. Legacy top-level facades now live under
     5→``desloppify.compat``.
     6→
     7→Structured namespaces are available under:
     8→- ``desloppify.core.discovery`` (api/impl)
     9→- ``desloppify.core.pathing`` (api/impl)
    10→- ``desloppify.core.io`` (api/impl)
    11→"""

    13→from __future__ import annotations
    14→
    15→import importlib
    16→
    17→__all__ = ["discovery", "io", "pathing"]
    18→
    19→_LAZY_SUBMODULES = {
    20→    "discovery": "desloppify.core.discovery",
    21→    "io": "desloppify.core.io",
    22→    "pathing": "desloppify.core.pathing",
    23→}
    24→
    25→
    26→def __getattr__(name: str):
    27→    target = _LAZY_SUBMODULES.get(name)
    28→    if target is None:
    29→        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    30→    value = importlib.import_module(target)
    31→    globals()[name] = value
    32→    return value
    33→

1→"""State filtering, ignore rules, and finding pattern matching."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import fnmatch
     6→import importlib
     7→
     8→__all__ = [
     9→    "finding_in_scan_scope",
    10→    "open_scope_breakdown",
    11→    "path_scoped_findings",
    12→    "is_ignored",
    13→    "matched_ignore_pattern",
    14→    "remove_ignored_findings",
    15→    "add_ignore",
    16→    "make_finding",
    17→]
    18→
    19→from desloppify.core.pathing.api import rel
    20→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import (
    21→    Finding,
    22→    StateModel,
    23→    ensure_state_defaults,
    24→    utc_now,
    25→    validate_state_invariants,

    27→
    28→
    29→def path_scoped_findings(
    30→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    31→    scan_path: str | None,
    32→) -> dict[str, Finding]:
    33→    """Filter findings to those within the given scan path."""
    34→    return {
    35→        finding_id: finding
    36→        for finding_id, finding in findings.items()
    37→        if finding_in_scan_scope(str(finding.get("file", "")), scan_path)
    38→    }
    39→
    40→
    41→def finding_in_scan_scope(file_path: str, scan_path: str | None) -> bool:
    42→    """Return True when a file path belongs to the active scan scope."""
    43→    if not scan_path or scan_path == ".":
    44→        return True
    45→    prefix = scan_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
    46→    return (
    47→        file_path.startswith(prefix)
    48→        or file_path == scan_path
    49→        or file_path == "."
    50→    )
    51→
    52→
    53→def open_scope_breakdown(
    54→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    55→    scan_path: str | None,
    56→    *,
    57→    detector: str | None = None,
    58→) -> dict[str, int]:
    59→    """Return open-finding counts split by in-scope vs out-of-scope carryover."""
    60→    in_scope = 0
    61→    out_of_scope = 0
    62→
    63→    for finding in findings.values():
    64→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    65→            continue
    66→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
    67→            continue
    68→        if detector is not None and finding.get("detector") != detector:
    69→            continue
    70→        file_path = str(finding.get("file", ""))
    71→        if finding_in_scan_scope(file_path, scan_path):
    72→            in_scope += 1
    73→        else:
    74→            out_of_scope += 1
    75→
    76→    return {
    77→        "in_scope": in_scope,
    78→        "out_of_scope": out_of_scope,
    79→        "global": in_scope + out_of_scope,
    80→    }
    81→
    82→
    83→def is_ignored(finding_id: str, file: str, ignore_patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    84→    """Check if a finding matches any ignore pattern (glob, ID prefix, or file path)."""
    85→    return matched_ignore_pattern(finding_id, file, ignore_patterns) is not None
    86→
    87→
    88→def matched_ignore_pattern(
    89→    finding_id: str, file: str, ignore_patterns: list[str]
    90→) -> str | None:
    91→    """Return the ignore pattern that matched, if any."""
    92→    for pattern in ignore_patterns:
    93→        if "*" in pattern:
    94→            target = finding_id if "::" in pattern else file
    95→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(target, pattern):
    96→                return pattern
    97→            continue
    98→
    99→        if "::" in pattern:
   100→            if finding_id.startswith(pattern):
   101→                return pattern
   102→            continue
   103→
   104→        if file == pattern or file == rel(pattern):
   105→            return pattern
   106→
   107→    return None
   108→
   109→
   110→def remove_ignored_findings(state: StateModel, pattern: str) -> int:
   111→    """Suppress findings matching an ignore pattern. Returns count affected."""
   112→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   113→    matched_ids = [
   114→        finding_id
   115→        for finding_id, finding in state["findings"].items()
   116→        if is_ignored(finding_id, finding["file"], [pattern])
   117→    ]
   118→    now = utc_now()
   119→    for finding_id in matched_ids:
   120→        finding = state["findings"][finding_id]
   121→        finding["suppressed"] = True
   122→        finding["suppressed_at"] = now
   123→        finding["suppression_pattern"] = pattern
   124→    scoring_mod = importlib.import_module("desloppify.engine._state.scoring")
   125→    scoring_mod._recompute_stats(state, scan_path=state.get("scan_path"))
   126→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   127→    return len(matched_ids)
   128→
   129→
   130→def add_ignore(state: StateModel, pattern: str) -> int:
   131→    """Add an ignore pattern and remove existing matching findings."""
   132→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   133→    config = state.setdefault("config", {})
   134→    ignores = config.setdefault("ignore", [])
   135→    if pattern not in ignores:
   136→        ignores.append(pattern)
   137→    return remove_ignored_findings(state, pattern)
   138→
   139→
   140→def make_finding(
   141→    detector: str,
   142→    file: str,
   143→    name: str,
   144→    *,
   145→    tier: int,
   146→    confidence: str,
   147→    summary: str,
   148→    detail: dict | None = None,
   149→) -> Finding:
   150→    """Create a normalized finding dict with a stable ID."""
   151→    rfile = rel(file)
   152→    finding_id = f"{detector}::{rfile}::{name}" if name else f"{detector}::{rfile}"
   153→    now = utc_now()
   154→    return {
   155→        "id": finding_id,
   156→        "detector": detector,
   157→        "file": rfile,
   158→        "tier": tier,
   159→        "confidence": confidence,
   160→        "summary": summary,
   161→        "detail": detail or {},
   162→        "status": "open",
   163→        "note": None,
   164→        "first_seen": now,
   165→        "last_seen": now,
   166→        "resolved_at": None,
   167→        "reopen_count": 0,
   168→    }
   169→
   170→
   171→def _matches_pattern(finding_id: str, finding: dict[str, str], pattern: str) -> bool:
   172→    """Check if a finding matches by ID, glob, prefix, detector, or path."""
   173→    return (
   174→        finding_id == pattern
   175→        or ("*" in pattern and fnmatch.fnmatch(finding_id, pattern))
   176→        or ("::" in pattern and finding_id.startswith(pattern))
   177→        or (
   178→            finding.get("detector") == pattern
   179→            or finding["file"] == pattern
   180→            or finding["file"].startswith(pattern.rstrip("/") + "/")
   181→        )
   182→    )
   183→

1→"""Terminal output helpers shared across commands.
     2→
     3→Implementation module for the ``desloppify.core.io`` namespace.
     4→"""
     5→
     6→from __future__ import annotations
     7→
     8→import json
     9→import os
    10→import sys
    11→from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
    12→from typing import Any
    13→
    14→LOC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD = 10000  # Switch from "1,234" to "1K" format
    15→
    16→COLORS = {
    17→    "reset": "\033[0m",
    18→    "bold": "\033[1m",
    19→    "dim": "\033[2m",
    20→    "red": "\033[31m",
    21→    "green": "\033[32m",
    22→    "yellow": "\033[33m",
    23→    "blue": "\033[34m",
    24→    "cyan": "\033[36m",
    25→}
    26→
    27→NO_COLOR = os.environ.get("NO_COLOR") is not None
    28→
    29→
    30→def colorize(text: str, color: str) -> str:
    31→    if NO_COLOR or not sys.stdout.isatty():
    32→        return str(text)
    33→    return f"{COLORS.get(color, '')}{text}{COLORS['reset']}"
    34→
    35→
    36→def log(msg: str) -> None:
    37→    """Print a dim status message to stderr."""
    38→    print(colorize(msg, "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
    39→
    40→
    41→def print_table(
    42→    headers: list[str], rows: list[list[str]], widths: list[int] | None = None
    43→) -> None:
    44→    if not rows:
    45→        return
    46→    if not widths:
    47→        widths = [
    48→            max(len(str(h)), *(len(str(r[i])) for r in rows))
    49→            for i, h in enumerate(headers)
    50→        ]
    51→    header_line = "  ".join(h.ljust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, widths, strict=False))
    52→    print(colorize(header_line, "bold"))
    53→    print(colorize("─" * (sum(widths) + 2 * (len(widths) - 1)), "dim"))
    54→    for row in rows:
    55→        print("  ".join(str(v).ljust(w) for v, w in zip(row, widths, strict=False)))
    56→
    57→
    58→def display_entries(
    59→    args: object,
    60→    entries: Sequence[Any],
    61→    *,
    62→    label: str,
    63→    empty_msg: str,
    64→    columns: Sequence[str],
    65→    widths: list[int] | None,
    66→    row_fn: Callable[[Any], list[str]],
    67→    json_payload: dict | None = None,
    68→    overflow: bool = True,
    69→) -> bool:
    70→    """Standard JSON/empty/table display for detect commands."""
    71→    if getattr(args, "json", False):
    72→        payload = json_payload or {"count": len(entries), "entries": entries}
    73→        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    74→        return True
    75→    if not entries:
    76→        print(colorize(empty_msg, "green"))
    77→        return False
    78→    print(colorize(f"\n{label}: {len(entries)}\n", "bold"))
    79→    top = getattr(args, "top", 20)
    80→    rows = [row_fn(e) for e in entries[:top]]
    81→    print_table(list(columns), rows, widths)
    82→    if overflow and len(entries) > top:
    83→        print(f"\n  ... and {len(entries) - top} more")
    84→    return True
    85→
    86→

    89→    "COLORS",
    90→    "NO_COLOR",
    91→    "colorize",
    92→    "display_entries",
    93→    "log",
    94→    "print_table",
    95→]
    96→

    82→class ScanStateContractError(ValueError):
    83→    """Raised when persisted scan state violates required runtime contracts."""
    84→
    85→
    86→def _state_subjective_assessments(
    87→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
    88→) -> dict[str, object]:
    89→    """Return normalized subjective assessment store from state."""
    90→    try:
    91→        return state_mod.require_subjective_assessments(state)
    92→    except ValueError as exc:
    93→        raise ScanStateContractError(
    94→            "state.subjective_assessments must be an object; rerun with a valid state file"
    95→        ) from exc
    96→
    97→
    98→def _state_lang_capabilities(
    99→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   100→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   101→    """Return normalized language capability map from state."""
   102→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
   103→    if capabilities is None:
   104→        normalized: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   105→        state["lang_capabilities"] = normalized
   106→        return normalized
   107→    if isinstance(capabilities, dict):
   108→        return capabilities
   109→    raise ScanStateContractError(
   110→        "state.lang_capabilities must be an object when present"
   111→    )
   112→

   114→def _state_findings(state: state_mod.StateModel) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
   115→    """Return normalized finding map from state."""
