   172→def _record_scan_warning(
   173→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   174→    *,
   175→    code: str,
   176→    message: str,
   177→    print_user_warning: bool = True,
   178→) -> None:
   179→    """Persist one structured scan warning and optionally print it."""
   180→    warnings = runtime.state.get("scan_warnings")
   181→    if not isinstance(warnings, list):
   182→        warnings = []
   183→        runtime.state["scan_warnings"] = warnings
   184→    warnings.append(
   185→        {
   186→            "code": code,
   187→            "message": message,
   188→            "recorded_at": state_mod.utc_now(),
   189→        }
   190→    )
   191→    if print_user_warning:
   192→        print(colorize(f"  Scan warning [{code}]: {message}", "yellow"))

   195→def _configure_lang_runtime(
   196→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   197→    config: dict[str, object],
   198→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   199→    lang: LangRun | None,
   200→) -> LangRun | None:
   201→    """Populate runtime context and threshold overrides for a selected language."""
   202→    if not lang:
   203→        return None
   204→
   205→    lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang)
   206→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(config, lang)
   207→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(
   208→        lang,
   209→        overrides=LangRunOverrides(
   210→            review_cache=state.get("review_cache", {}),
   211→            review_max_age_days=config.get("review_max_age_days", 30),
   212→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,
   213→            runtime_options=lang_options,
   214→            large_threshold_override=config.get("large_files_threshold", 0),
   215→            props_threshold_override=config.get("props_threshold", 0),
   216→        ),
   217→    )
   218→
   219→    lang_capabilities = _state_lang_capabilities(state)
   220→    lang_capabilities[runtime_lang.name] = {
   221→        "fixers": sorted(runtime_lang.fixers.keys()),
   222→        "typecheck_cmd": runtime_lang.typecheck_cmd,
   223→    }
   224→    return runtime_lang

   227→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   228→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   229→    *,
   230→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   231→) -> int:
   232→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   233→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   234→
   235→    reset_keys = {
   236→        key.strip()
   237→        for key in assessments
   238→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   239→    }
   240→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   241→
   242→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   243→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   244→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   245→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   246→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   247→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   248→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   249→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   250→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   251→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   252→            payload.pop("components", None)
   253→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   254→            continue
   255→        assessments[key] = {
   256→            "score": 0.0,
   257→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   258→            "assessed_at": now,
   259→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   260→            "placeholder": True,
   261→        }
   262→    return len(reset_keys)
   263→
   264→
   265→def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   266→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   267→) -> int:
   268→    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
   269→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   270→
   271→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   272→    expired = 0
   273→    for payload in assessments.values():
   274→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   275→            continue
   276→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
   277→            continue
   278→        payload["score"] = 0.0
   279→        payload["source"] = "manual_override_expired"
   280→        payload["assessed_at"] = now
   281→        payload["reset_by"] = "manual_override_expired"
   282→        payload["placeholder"] = True
   283→        payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   284→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   285→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   286→        payload.pop("components", None)
   287→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   288→        expired += 1
   289→    return expired

   292→def prepare_scan_runtime(args) -> ScanRuntime:
   293→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   294→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   295→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   296→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   297→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)
   298→    path = Path(args.path)
   299→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   300→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   301→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   302→    expired_manual_override_count = _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   303→        state
   304→    )
   305→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   306→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   307→            state,
   308→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   309→        )
   310→
   311→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   312→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   313→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   314→
   315→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   316→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   317→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   318→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   319→
   320→    return ScanRuntime(
   321→        args=args,
   322→        state_path=state_file,
   323→        state=state,
   324→        project_root=get_project_root(),
   325→        path=path,
   326→        config=config,
   327→        lang=lang,
   328→        lang_label=f" ({lang.name})" if lang else "",
   329→        profile=profile,
   330→        effective_include_slow=effective_include_slow,
   331→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   332→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   333→        expired_manual_override_count=expired_manual_override_count,
   334→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   335→    )

   338→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(
   339→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   340→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   341→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   342→    """Append stale exclude findings when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   343→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   344→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   345→        return findings
   346→
   347→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   348→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   349→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, runtime.project_root
   350→    )
   351→    if not stale:
   352→        return findings
   353→
   354→    augmented = list(findings)
   355→    augmented.extend(stale)
   356→    for stale_finding in stale:
   357→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_finding['summary']}", "dim"))
   358→    return augmented

   377→def run_scan_generation(
   378→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   379→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   380→    """Run detector pipeline and return findings, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   381→    with file_cache_scope():
   382→        with parse_cache_scope():
   383→            findings, potentials = plan_mod.generate_findings(
   384→                runtime.path,
   385→                lang=runtime.lang,
   386→                options=PlanScanOptions(
   387→                    include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   388→                    zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   389→                    profile=runtime.profile,
   390→                ),
   391→            )
   392→
   393→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   394→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   395→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   396→    )
   397→    findings = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(findings, runtime)
   398→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   399→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   400→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   401→    )
   402→    findings, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   403→        findings,
   404→        runtime,
   405→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   406→    )
   407→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   408→    return findings, potentials, codebase_metrics
   409→

   411→def merge_scan_results(
   412→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   413→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   414→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   415→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   416→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   417→    """Merge findings into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   418→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   419→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   420→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   421→
   422→    if not path_changed:
   423→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   424→    else:
   425→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   426→    prev_dim_scores = (
   427→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   428→    )
   429→
   430→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   431→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   432→    runtime.state["plan_sync_failed"] = False
   433→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   434→
   435→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   436→
   437→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   438→        runtime.state,
   439→        findings,
   440→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   441→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   442→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   443→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   444→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   445→            potentials=potentials,
   446→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   447→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   448→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   449→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   450→        ),
   451→    )
   452→
   453→    issues_mod.expire_stale_holistic(
   454→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   455→    )
   456→    state_mod.save_state(
   457→        runtime.state,
   458→        runtime.state_path,
   459→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   460→    )
   461→
   462→    # Clear needs_rescan flag after successful scan merge (best-effort)
   463→    if runtime.config.get("needs_rescan"):
   464→        try:
   465→            runtime.config["needs_rescan"] = False
   466→            _save_config(runtime.config)
   467→        except OSError as exc:
   468→            logger.debug("Failed to clear config.needs_rescan: %s", exc)
   469→            _record_scan_warning(
   470→                runtime,
   471→                code="config_persist_failed",
   472→                message=f"could not persist scan config updates ({exc})",
   473→            )
   474→
   475→    _reconcile_plan_best_effort(runtime)
   476→
   477→    return ScanMergeResult(
   478→        diff=diff,
   479→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   480→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   481→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   482→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   483→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   484→    )
   485→
   486→
   487→def _reconcile_plan_best_effort(runtime: ScanRuntime) -> None:
   488→    """Reconcile plan state after scan with typed warning/error handling."""
   489→    plan_path = runtime.state_path.parent / "plan.json" if runtime.state_path else None
   490→    try:
   491→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   492→        dirty = _reconcile_existing_plan(runtime, plan)
   493→        dirty = _sync_unscored_dimensions(runtime, plan) or dirty
   494→        dirty = _sync_stale_dimension_queue(runtime, plan) or dirty
   495→        dirty = auto_cluster_findings(plan, runtime.state) or dirty
   496→        if dirty:
   497→            save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   498→    except _PLAN_SYNC_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   499→        runtime.state["plan_sync_failed"] = True
   500→        logger.warning("Plan reconciliation skipped due to runtime error: %s", exc)
   501→        _record_scan_warning(
   502→            runtime,
   503→            code="plan_sync_failed",
   504→            message=f"plan reconciliation skipped ({exc})",
   505→        )
   506→    except _PLAN_SYNC_UNEXPECTED_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   507→        runtime.state["plan_sync_failed"] = True
   508→        logger.warning(
   509→            "Plan reconciliation skipped due to unexpected error: %s",
   510→            exc,
   511→            exc_info=True,
   512→        )
   513→        _record_scan_warning(
   514→            runtime,
   515→            code="plan_sync_failed_unexpected",
   516→            message=f"plan reconciliation skipped due to unexpected error ({exc})",
   517→        )
   518→

   520→def _plan_has_user_content(plan: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
   521→    return bool(
   522→        plan.get("queue_order")
   523→        or plan.get("overrides")
   524→        or plan.get("clusters")
   525→        or plan.get("skipped")
   526→    )
   527→
   528→
   529→def _reconcile_existing_plan(runtime: ScanRuntime, plan: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
   530→    if not _plan_has_user_content(plan):
   531→        return False
   532→    recon = reconcile_plan_after_scan(plan, runtime.state)
   533→    if recon.resurfaced:
   534→        print(
   535→            colorize(
   536→                f"  Plan: {len(recon.resurfaced)} skipped item(s) re-surfaced after review period.",
   537→                "cyan",
   538→            )
   539→        )
   540→    return bool(recon.changes)
   541→

   543→def _sync_unscored_dimensions(runtime: ScanRuntime, plan: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
   544→    unscored_sync = sync_unscored_dimensions(plan, runtime.state)
   545→    if unscored_sync.injected:
   546→        print(
   547→            colorize(
   548→                f"  Plan: {len(unscored_sync.injected)} unscored subjective dimension(s) queued for initial review.",
   549→                "cyan",
   550→            )
   551→        )
   552→    return bool(unscored_sync.changes)

   555→def _sync_stale_dimension_queue(runtime: ScanRuntime, plan: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
   556→    dim_sync = sync_stale_dimensions(plan, runtime.state)
   557→    if dim_sync.pruned:
   558→        print(

   561→                "cyan",
   562→            )
   563→        )
   564→    if dim_sync.injected:
   565→        print(
   566→            colorize(
   567→                f"  Plan: {len(dim_sync.injected)} stale subjective dimension(s) queued for refresh.",
   568→                "cyan",
   569→            )
   570→        )
   571→    return bool(dim_sync.changes)

   574→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   575→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   576→    config: dict[str, object],
   577→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   578→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden finding counters."""
   579→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   580→        state_mod.resolve_finding_noise_settings(config)
   581→    )
   582→    findings_by_id = _state_findings(state)
   583→    open_findings = [
   584→        finding
   585→        for finding in state_mod.path_scoped_findings(
   586→            findings_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   587→        ).values()
   588→        if finding.get("status") == "open"
   589→    ]
   590→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_finding_noise_budget(
   591→        open_findings,
   592→        budget=noise_budget,
   593→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   594→    )
   595→
   596→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   597→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   598→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   599→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   600→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   601→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   602→    )
   603→
   604→
   605→def persist_reminder_history(
   606→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   607→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   608→) -> None:
   609→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   610→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   611→        return
   612→
   613→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   614→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   615→    state_mod.save_state(
   616→        runtime.state,
   617→        runtime.state_path,
   618→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   619→    )
   620→
   621→
   622→__all__ = [
   623→    "ScanStateContractError",
   624→    "ScanMergeResult",
   625→    "ScanNoiseSnapshot",
   626→    "ScanRuntime",
   627→    "merge_scan_results",
   628→    "persist_reminder_history",
   629→    "prepare_scan_runtime",
   630→    "resolve_noise_snapshot",
   631→    "run_scan_generation",
   632→]

    57→def phase_logs(path: Path, lang: LangRun) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
    58→    log_result = logs_detector_mod.detect_logs_result(path)

    61→    log_groups: dict[tuple, list] = defaultdict(list)
    62→    for e in log_entries:
    63→        log_groups[(e["file"], e["tag"])].append(e)
    64→    results = []
    65→    for (file, tag), entries in log_groups.items():
    66→        results.append(
    67→            make_finding(
    68→                "logs",
    69→                file,
    70→                tag,
    71→                tier=1,
    72→                confidence="high",
    73→                summary=f"{len(entries)} tagged logs [{tag}]",
    74→                detail={
    75→                    "count": len(entries),
    76→                    "lines": [e["line"] for e in entries[:20]],
    77→                },
    78→            )
    79→        )
    80→    log(f"         {len(log_entries)} instances → {len(results)} findings")
    81→    return results, {"logs": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_files)}

   149→            extra.append(

   158→    results, potentials = run_structural_phase(
   159→        path,

   227→def _make_boundary_findings(
   228→    single_use_findings: list[dict],
   229→    path: Path,
   230→    graph: dict,
   231→    lang: LangRun,
   232→    shared_prefix: str,
   233→    tools_prefix: str,
   234→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   235→    """Create boundary-candidate findings, deduplicated against single-use."""
   236→    single_use_emitted = {
   237→        rel(str(finding.get("file", "")))
   238→        for finding in single_use_findings
   239→        if finding.get("detector") == "single_use" and finding.get("file")
   240→    }
   241→
   242→    results = []
   243→    deduped = 0
   244→    boundary_entries, total_shared = coupling_detector_mod.detect_boundary_candidates(
   245→        path,
   246→        graph,
   247→        shared_prefix=shared_prefix,
   248→        tools_prefix=tools_prefix,
   249→        skip_basenames={"index.ts", "index.tsx"},
   250→    )
   251→    for e in boundary_entries:
   252→        if rel(e["file"]) in single_use_emitted:
   253→            deduped += 1
   254→            continue
   255→        results.append(
   256→            make_finding(
   257→                "coupling",
   258→                e["file"],
   259→                f"boundary::{e['sole_tool']}",
   260→                tier=3,
   261→                confidence="medium",
   262→                summary=f"Boundary candidate ({e['loc']} LOC): only used by {e['sole_tool']} "
   263→                f"({e['importer_count']} importers)",
   264→                detail={
   265→                    "sole_tool": e["sole_tool"],
   266→                    "importer_count": e["importer_count"],
   267→                    "loc": e["loc"],
   268→                },
   269→            )
   270→        )
   271→    if deduped:
   272→        log(f"         ({deduped} boundary candidates skipped — covered by single_use)")
   273→    return results, total_shared

   276→def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRun) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   277→    graph = deps_detector_mod.build_dep_graph(path)
   278→    zm = lang.zone_map
   279→
   280→    shared_results, shared_potentials = run_coupling_phase(
   281→        path,
   282→        lang,
   283→        build_dep_graph_fn=lambda _path: graph,
   284→        log_fn=log,
   285→        single_use_skip_dir_names={"commands"},
   286→        orphaned_options=orphaned_detector_mod.OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   287→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   288→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   289→            dynamic_import_finder=deps_detector_mod.build_dynamic_import_targets,
   290→            alias_resolver=deps_detector_mod.ts_alias_resolver,
   291→        ),
   292→    )
   293→    results = list(shared_results)
   294→
   295→    src_path = get_src_path()
   296→    shared_prefix = f"{src_path}/shared/"
   297→    tools_prefix = f"{src_path}/tools/"
   298→    coupling_entries, coupling_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_coupling_violations(
   299→        path, graph, shared_prefix=shared_prefix, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   300→    )
   301→    coupling_entries = filter_entries(zm, coupling_entries, "coupling")
   302→    for e in coupling_entries:
   303→        results.append(
   304→            make_finding(
   305→                "coupling",
   306→                e["file"],
   307→                e["target"],
   308→                tier=2,
   309→                confidence="high",
   310→                summary=f"Backwards coupling: shared imports {e['target']} (tool: {e['tool']})",
   311→                detail={
   312→                    "target": e["target"],
   313→                    "tool": e["tool"],
   314→                    "direction": e["direction"],
   315→                },
   316→            )
   317→        )
   318→
   319→    # TS-specific: boundary candidates (deduplicated against single-use)
   320→    boundary_findings, _ = _make_boundary_findings(
   321→        shared_results, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   322→    )
   323→    results.extend(boundary_findings)
   324→
   325→    # TS-specific: cross-tool imports
   326→    cross_tool, cross_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_cross_tool_imports(
   327→        path, graph, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   328→    )
   329→    cross_tool = filter_entries(zm, cross_tool, "coupling")
   330→    for e in cross_tool:
   331→        results.append(
   332→            make_finding(
   333→                "coupling",
   334→                e["file"],
   335→                e["target"],
   336→                tier=2,
   337→                confidence="high",
   338→                summary=f"Cross-tool import: {e['source_tool']}→{e['target_tool']} ({e['target']})",
   339→                detail={
   340→                    "target": e["target"],
   341→                    "source_tool": e["source_tool"],
   342→                    "target_tool": e["target_tool"],
   343→                    "direction": e["direction"],
   344→                },
   345→            )
   346→        )
   347→    if cross_tool:
   348→        log(f"         cross-tool: {len(cross_tool)} imports")
   349→
   350→    # Re-export facades (shared detector)
   351→    facade_entries, _ = facade_detector_mod.detect_reexport_facades(graph)
   352→    facade_entries = filter_entries(zm, facade_entries, "facade")
   353→    results.extend(make_facade_findings(facade_entries, log))
   354→
   355→    # TS-specific: pattern consistency
   356→    pattern_result = patterns_detector_mod.detect_pattern_anomalies_result(path)
   357→    pattern_entries = pattern_result.entries
   358→    total_areas = pattern_result.population_size
   359→    for e in pattern_entries:
   360→        results.append(
   361→            make_finding(
   362→                "patterns",
   363→                e["area"],
   364→                e["family"],
   365→                tier=3,
   366→                confidence=e.get("confidence", "low"),
   367→                summary=f"Competing patterns ({e['family']}): {e['review'][:120]}",
   368→                detail={
   369→                    "family": e["family"],
   370→                    "patterns_used": e["patterns_used"],
   371→                    "pattern_count": e["pattern_count"],
   372→                    "review": e["review"],
   373→                },
   374→            )
   375→        )
   376→
   377→    # TS-specific: naming consistency
   378→    naming_entries, total_dirs = naming_detector_mod.detect_naming_inconsistencies(
   379→        path,
   380→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   381→        skip_names=TS_SKIP_NAMES,
   382→        skip_dirs=TS_SKIP_DIRS,
   383→    )
   384→    for e in naming_entries:
   385→        results.append(
   386→            make_finding(
   387→                "naming",
   388→                e["directory"],
   389→                e["minority"],
   390→                tier=3,
   391→                confidence="low",
   392→                summary=f"Naming inconsistency: {e['minority_count']} {e['minority']} files "
   393→                f"in {e['majority']}-majority dir ({e['total_files']} total)",
   394→                detail={
   395→                    "majority": e["majority"],
   396→                    "majority_count": e["majority_count"],
   397→                    "minority": e["minority"],
   398→                    "minority_count": e["minority_count"],
   399→                    "outliers": e["outliers"],
   400→                },
   401→            )
   402→        )
   403→    log(f"         → {len(results)} coupling/structural findings total")
   404→    coupling_edges = coupling_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   405→    cross_edges = cross_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   406→    potentials = dict(shared_potentials)
   407→    potentials["coupling"] = coupling_edges + cross_edges
   408→    potentials["patterns"] = total_areas
   409→    potentials["naming"] = total_dirs
   410→    potentials["facade"] = int(shared_potentials.get("orphaned", 0))
   411→    return results, potentials

   414→def phase_smells(path: Path, lang: LangRun) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   415→    smell_entries, total_smell_files = smells_detector_mod.detect_smells(path)

   494→                    "line": e["line"],
   495→                },
   496→            )
   497→        )
   498→    if hook_entries:
   499→        log(f"         react: {len(hook_entries)} bloated hook returns")
   500→
   501→    # TS-specific: Boolean state explosion
   502→    bool_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_boolean_state_explosion(path)
   503→    for e in bool_entries:
   504→        states_str = ", ".join(e["states"][:5])
   505→        results.append(
   506→            make_finding(
   507→                "react",
   508→                e["file"],
   509→                f"bool_state::{e['prefix']}",
   510→                tier=3,
   511→                confidence="low",
   512→                summary=f"Boolean state explosion: {e['count']} boolean useState hooks ({states_str})",
   513→                detail={
   514→                    "count": e["count"],
   515→                    "setters": e["setters"],
   516→                    "states": e["states"],
   517→                    "line": e["line"],
   518→                },
   519→            )
   520→        )
   521→    if bool_entries:
   522→        log(f"         react: {len(bool_entries)} boolean state explosions")
   523→
   524→    return results, {
   525→        "smells": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_smell_files),
   526→        "react": total_effects,
   527→    }
   528→

   534→_phase_deprecated = phase_deprecated

     2→
     3→Implementation module for the ``desloppify.core.discovery`` namespace.
     4→"""
     5→
     6→from __future__ import annotations
     7→
     8→import os
     9→from collections.abc import Iterator
    10→from contextlib import contextmanager
    11→from pathlib import Path

    13→from desloppify.core.file_paths import matches_exclusion

    21→from desloppify.core.runtime_state import current_runtime_context
    22→
    23→# Directories that are never useful to scan — always pruned during traversal.
    24→DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = frozenset(
    25→    {
    26→        "node_modules",
    27→        ".git",
    28→        "__pycache__",
    29→        ".venv",
    30→        ".venv*",
    31→        "venv",
    32→        ".env",
    33→        "dist",
    34→        "build",
    35→        ".next",
    36→        ".nuxt",
    37→        ".output",
    38→        ".tox",
    39→        ".mypy_cache",
    40→        ".pytest_cache",
    41→        ".ruff_cache",
    42→        ".eggs",
    43→        "*.egg-info",
    44→        ".svn",
    45→        ".hg",
    46→    }
    47→)
    48→
    49→
    50→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    51→    """Set global exclusion patterns (called once from CLI at startup)."""
    52→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    53→    runtime.exclusions = tuple(patterns)
    54→    runtime.source_file_cache.clear()
    55→
    56→
    57→def get_exclusions() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    58→    """Return current extra exclusion patterns."""
    59→    return current_runtime_context().exclusions
    60→
    61→
    62→def enable_file_cache() -> None:
    63→    """Enable scan-scoped file content cache."""
    64→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    65→    runtime.file_text_cache.enable()
    66→    runtime.cache_enabled = True
    67→
    68→
    69→def disable_file_cache() -> None:
    70→    """Disable file content cache and free memory."""
    71→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    72→    runtime.file_text_cache.disable()
    73→    runtime.cache_enabled = False
    74→
    75→
    76→def is_file_cache_enabled() -> bool:
    77→    """Return whether scan-scoped file cache is currently enabled."""
    78→    return current_runtime_context().cache_enabled
    79→
    80→
    81→@contextmanager
    82→def file_cache_scope() -> Iterator[None]:
    83→    """Enable file cache for one scope and restore prior state on exit."""
    84→    was_enabled = is_file_cache_enabled()
    85→    if not was_enabled:
    86→        enable_file_cache()
    87→    try:
    88→        yield
    89→    finally:
    90→        if not was_enabled:
    91→            disable_file_cache()
    92→
    93→
    94→def read_file_text(filepath: str) -> str | None:
    95→    """Read a file as text, with optional caching."""
    96→    return current_runtime_context().file_text_cache.read(filepath)
    97→
    98→
    99→def clear_source_file_cache_for_tests() -> None:
   100→    current_runtime_context().source_file_cache.clear()
   101→
   102→
   103→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
   104→    """All exclusion directories as absolute paths, for passing to external tools.
   105→
   106→    Combines DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (non-glob entries) + get_exclusions() (runtime/config),
   107→    resolves each against *scan_root*. Filters out glob patterns (``*`` in name)
   108→    since most CLI tools want plain directory paths.
   109→    """
   110→    patterns = set()
   111→    for pat in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS:
   112→        if "*" not in pat:
   113→            patterns.add(pat)
   114→    patterns.update(p for p in get_exclusions() if p and "*" not in p)
   115→    return [str(scan_root / p) for p in sorted(patterns) if p]
   116→
   117→
   118→def _is_excluded_dir(name: str, rel_path: str, extra: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
   119→    in_default_exclusions = name in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS or name.endswith(".egg-info")
   120→    is_virtualenv_dir = name.startswith(".venv") or name.startswith("venv")
   121→    matches_extra_exclusion = bool(
   122→        extra
   123→        and any(
   124→            matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion)
   125→            or exclusion == name
   126→            or exclusion == name + "/**"
   127→            or exclusion == name + "/*"
   128→            for exclusion in extra
   129→        )
   130→    )
   131→    return in_default_exclusions or is_virtualenv_dir or matches_extra_exclusion
   132→
   133→
   134→def _find_source_files_cached(
   135→    path: str,
   136→    extensions: tuple[str, ...],
   137→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
   138→    extra_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   139→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   140→    """Cached file discovery using os.walk with traversal-time pruning."""
   141→    cache_key = (path, extensions, exclusions, extra_exclusions)
   142→    cache = current_runtime_context().source_file_cache
   143→    cached = cache.get(cache_key)
   144→    if cached is not None:
   145→        return cached
   146→
   147→    project_root = _text_utils.get_project_root()
   148→    root = Path(path)
   149→    if not root.is_absolute():
   150→        root = project_root / root
   151→    all_exclusions = (exclusions or ()) + extra_exclusions
   152→    ext_set = set(extensions)
   153→    files: list[str] = []
   154→    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
   155→        rel_dir = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(dirpath, project_root))
   156→        dirnames[:] = sorted(
   157→            d
   158→            for d in dirnames
   159→            if not _is_excluded_dir(d, rel_dir + "/" + d, all_exclusions)
   160→        )
   161→        for fname in filenames:
   162→            if any(fname.endswith(ext) for ext in ext_set):
   163→                full = os.path.join(dirpath, fname)
   164→                rel_file = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(full, project_root))
   165→                if all_exclusions and any(
   166→                    matches_exclusion(rel_file, ex) for ex in all_exclusions
   167→                ):
   168→                    continue
   169→                files.append(rel_file)
   170→    result = tuple(sorted(files))
   171→    cache.put(cache_key, result)
   172→    return result
   173→
   174→
   175→def find_source_files(
   176→    path: str | Path, extensions: list[str], exclusions: list[str] | None = None
   177→) -> list[str]:
   178→    """Find all files with given extensions under a path, excluding patterns."""
   179→    return list(
   180→        _find_source_files_cached(
   181→            str(path),
   182→            tuple(extensions),
   183→            tuple(exclusions) if exclusions else None,
   184→            get_exclusions(),
   185→        )
   186→    )
   187→
   188→
   189→def find_ts_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   190→    return find_source_files(path, [".ts", ".tsx"])
   191→
   192→
   193→def find_tsx_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   194→    return find_source_files(path, [".tsx"])
   195→
   196→
   197→def find_py_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   198→    return find_source_files(path, [".py"])
   199→
   200→
   201→__all__ = [
   202→    "DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS",
   203→    "collect_exclude_dirs",
   204→    "set_exclusions",
   205→    "get_exclusions",
   206→    "enable_file_cache",
   207→    "disable_file_cache",
   208→    "is_file_cache_enabled",
   209→    "read_file_text",
   210→    "clear_source_file_cache_for_tests",
   211→    "find_source_files",
   212→    "find_ts_files",
   213→    "find_tsx_files",
   214→    "find_py_files",
   215→    "file_cache_scope",
   216→]
   217→

1→"""Path resolution and exclusion matching helpers.
     2→
     3→Implementation module for the ``desloppify.core.pathing`` namespace.
     4→"""
     5→
     6→from __future__ import annotations
     7→
     8→import os
     9→import tempfile
    10→from fnmatch import fnmatch
    11→from pathlib import Path
    12→
    13→from desloppify.core._internal import text_utils as _text_utils
    14→
    15→
    16→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    17→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    18→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    19→    if exclusion in parts:
    20→        return True
    21→    if "*" in exclusion:
    22→        if any(fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    23→            return True
    24→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    25→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    26→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    27→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    28→            if fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    29→                return True
    30→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    31→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    32→        return rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    33→            normalized + os.sep
    34→        )
    35→    return False
    36→
    37→
    38→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    39→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    40→
    41→
    42→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    43→    try:
    44→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    45→    except ValueError:
    46→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    47→
    48→
    49→def rel(path: str) -> str:
    50→    root = _text_utils.get_project_root()
    51→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    52→    try:
    53→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    54→    except ValueError:
    55→        return normalize_path_separators(safe_relpath(resolved, root))
    56→
    57→
    58→def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    59→    """Resolve a filepath to absolute, handling both relative and absolute."""
    60→    p = Path(filepath)
    61→    if p.is_absolute():
    62→        return str(p.resolve())
    63→    return str((_text_utils.get_project_root() / filepath).resolve())
    64→
    65→
    66→def resolve_scan_file(
    67→    filepath: str | Path,
    68→    *,
    69→    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
    70→) -> Path:
    71→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    72→
    73→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    74→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    75→    """
    76→    p = Path(filepath)
    77→    if p.is_absolute():
    78→        return p.resolve()
    79→
    80→    root = _text_utils.get_project_root()
    81→    if scan_root is not None:
    82→        scan_root_path = Path(scan_root)
    83→        scan_root_abs = (
    84→            scan_root_path.resolve()
    85→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()
    86→            else (root / scan_root_path).resolve()
    87→        )
    88→        scan_candidate = (scan_root_abs / p).resolve()
    89→        if scan_candidate.exists():
    90→            return scan_candidate
    91→
    92→    return (root / p).resolve()
    93→
    94→
    95→def safe_write_text(filepath: str | Path, content: str) -> None:
    96→    """Atomically write text to a file using temp+rename."""
    97→    p = Path(filepath)
    98→    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    99→    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=p.parent, suffix=".tmp")
   100→    try:
   101→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
   102→            f.write(content)
   103→        os.replace(tmp, str(p))
   104→    except OSError:
   105→        if os.path.exists(tmp):
   106→            os.unlink(tmp)
   107→        raise
   108→
   109→
   110→__all__ = [

   112→    "normalize_path_separators",
   113→    "rel",
   114→    "resolve_path",
   115→    "resolve_scan_file",
   116→    "safe_relpath",
   117→    "safe_write_text",
   118→]

1→"""Detect module-level mutable state modified from functions within the same module."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→import logging
     7→import re
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.core.pathing.api import PROJECT_ROOT
    11→from desloppify.core.discovery.api import find_py_files
    12→
    13→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    14→
    15→
    16→# Mutable initializer values
    17→_MUTABLE_INIT = (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set)
    18→_MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES = {"set", "list", "dict", "defaultdict", "OrderedDict", "Counter"}
    19→
    20→# Mutating method names
    21→_MUTATING_METHODS = {
    22→    "append",
    23→    "extend",
    24→    "insert",
    25→    "pop",
    26→    "remove",
    27→    "clear",
    28→    "update",
    29→    "setdefault",
    30→    "add",
    31→    "discard",
    32→}
    33→
    34→
    35→def _is_mutable_init(value: ast.AST) -> bool:
    36→    """Check if an AST value is a mutable initializer ([], {}, set(), etc.)."""
    37→    if isinstance(value, _MUTABLE_INIT):
    38→        return True
    39→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    40→        func = value.func
    41→        if isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    42→            return True
    43→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    44→            return True
    45→    if isinstance(value, ast.Constant) and value.value is None:
    46→        return True
    47→    return False
    48→
    49→
    50→def _is_upper_case(name: str) -> bool:
    51→    """Check if a name is UPPER_CASE (constant convention)."""
    52→    return bool(re.match(r"^_?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$", name))
    53→
    54→
    55→def _mutable_name_from_assign_target(target: ast.AST, value: ast.AST) -> str | None:
    56→    if not isinstance(target, ast.Name):
    57→        return None
    58→    if _is_upper_case(target.id):
    59→        return None
    60→    if not _is_mutable_init(value):
    61→        return None
    62→    return target.id
    63→
    64→
    65→def _mutable_name_from_ann_assign(stmt: ast.AnnAssign) -> str | None:
    66→    if not isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name):
    67→        return None
    68→    name = stmt.target.id
    69→    if _is_upper_case(name):
    70→        return None
    71→    if stmt.value is not None and _is_mutable_init(stmt.value):
    72→        return name
    73→    if _is_optional_annotation(stmt.annotation):
    74→        return name
    75→    return None
    76→
    77→
    78→def _collect_module_level_mutables(tree: ast.Module) -> dict[str, int]:
    79→    """Collect module-level names initialized to mutable values.
    80→
    81→    Returns {name: lineno} for names that are NOT UPPER_CASE constants.
    82→    """
    83→    mutables: dict[str, int] = {}
    84→    for stmt in tree.body:
    85→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
    86→            for target in stmt.targets:
    87→                name = _mutable_name_from_assign_target(target, stmt.value)
    88→                if name:
    89→                    mutables[name] = stmt.lineno
    90→            continue
    91→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign):
    92→            name = _mutable_name_from_ann_assign(stmt)
    93→            if name:
    94→                mutables[name] = stmt.lineno
    95→    return mutables
    96→
    97→
    98→def _is_optional_annotation(ann: ast.AST) -> bool:
    99→    """Check if an annotation looks like Optional[...]."""
   100→    is_optional_subscript = isinstance(ann, ast.Subscript) and (
   101→        (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Name) and ann.value.id == "Optional")
   102→        or (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Attribute) and ann.value.attr == "Optional")
   103→    )
   104→    is_optional_union = (
   105→        isinstance(ann, ast.BinOp)
   106→        and isinstance(ann.op, ast.BitOr)
   107→        and (
   108→            (isinstance(ann.right, ast.Constant) and ann.right.value is None)
   109→            or (isinstance(ann.left, ast.Constant) and ann.left.value is None)
   110→        )
   111→    )
   112→    return is_optional_subscript or is_optional_union
   113→
   114→
   115→def _find_mutations_in_functions(
   116→    tree: ast.Module, mutables: dict[str, int]
   117→) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
   118→    """Find functions that reassign or mutate module-level mutable names.
   119→
   120→    Returns {name: [line numbers where mutation occurs]}.
   121→
   122→    Bare assignments (name = x) and augmented assignments (name += x) only count
   123→    as mutations when the function has an explicit `global name` declaration —
   124→    without it, Python creates a local variable. Subscript assignments (name[k] = v)
   125→    and method calls (name.append(x)) don't need `global` because they operate on
   126→    the object reference, not rebind the name.
   127→    """
   128→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
   129→
   130→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   131→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   132→            continue
   133→        param_names = _function_param_names(node)
   134→        global_names = _function_global_names(node)
   135→        _record_function_mutations(
   136→            node,
   137→            mutables=mutables,
   138→            param_names=param_names,
   139→            global_names=global_names,
   140→            mutations=mutations,
   141→        )
   142→
   143→    return mutations
   144→
   145→
   146→def _detect_in_module(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, entries: list[dict]):
   147→    """Detect global mutable config patterns in a single module."""
   148→    mutables = _collect_module_level_mutables(tree)
   149→    if not mutables:
   150→        return
   151→
   152→    mutations = _find_mutations_in_functions(tree, mutables)
   153→    if not mutations:
   154→        return
   155→
   156→    for name, mutation_lines in mutations.items():
   157→        defn_line = mutables[name]
   158→        entries.append(
   159→            {
   160→                "file": filepath,
   161→                "name": name,
   162→                "line": defn_line,
   163→                "mutation_lines": mutation_lines[:5],
   164→                "mutation_count": len(mutation_lines),
   165→                "confidence": "medium",
   166→                "summary": (
   167→                    f"Module-level mutable '{name}' (line {defn_line}) "
   168→                    f"modified from {len(mutation_lines)} site(s)"
   169→                ),
   170→            }
   171→        )
   172→
   173→
   174→# ── Import-binding footgun detection ─────────────────────
   175→
   176→
   177→def _detect_stale_imports(
   178→    path: Path,
   179→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]],
   180→    entries: list[dict],
   181→):
   182→    """Detect ``from X import mutable_name`` that creates a stale binding.
   183→
   184→    When a module-level mutable is reassigned (via ``global``), other modules
   185→    that import the name directly get a stale copy.  They should import the
   186→    module and access the attribute at call time instead.
   187→    """
   188→    files = find_py_files(path)
   189→
   190→    for filepath in files:
   191→        tree = _parse_python_tree(filepath, pass_name="stale-import")
   192→        if tree is None:
   193→            continue
   194→        _append_stale_import_entries(filepath, tree, mutated_names, entries)
   195→
   196→
   197→def detect_global_mutable_config(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   198→    """Detect module-level mutable state that gets modified from functions.
   199→
   200→    Also detects stale import bindings: other modules that `from X import name`
   201→    a mutable that gets reassigned, which creates a stale copy.
   202→
   203→    Returns (entries, total_files_checked).
   204→    """
   205→    files = find_py_files(path)
   206→    entries: list[dict] = []
   207→
   208→    # Phase 1: collect mutated globals per module
   209→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]] = {}  # {module_path: {name, ...}}
   210→
   211→    for filepath in files:
   212→        tree = _parse_python_tree(filepath, pass_name="mutable-state")
   213→        if tree is None:
   214→            continue
   215→
   216→        _detect_in_module(filepath, tree, entries)
   217→
   218→        # Track which modules have reassigned globals (need `global` keyword)
   219→        mutables = _collect_module_level_mutables(tree)
   220→        if not mutables:
   221→            continue
   222→        reassigned = _collect_reassigned_globals(tree, mutables)
   223→        if reassigned:
   224→            mutated_names[_module_path_from_file(filepath)] = reassigned
   225→
   226→    # Phase 2: detect stale import bindings
   227→    if mutated_names:
   228→        _detect_stale_imports(path, mutated_names, entries)
   229→
   230→    return entries, len(files)
   231→
   232→
   233→def _function_param_names(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> set[str]:
   234→    return {a.arg for a in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs}
   235→
   236→
   237→def _function_global_names(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> set[str]:
   238→    names: set[str] = set()
   239→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   240→        if isinstance(child, ast.Global):
   241→            names.update(child.names)
   242→    return names
   243→
   244→
   245→def _record_name_assignment(
   246→    target: ast.Name,
   247→    *,
   248→    lineno: int,
   249→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   250→    param_names: set[str],
   251→    global_names: set[str],
   252→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   253→) -> None:
   254→    if target.id not in mutables:
   255→        return
   256→    if target.id in param_names or target.id not in global_names:
   257→        return
   258→    mutations.setdefault(target.id, []).append(lineno)
   259→
   260→
   261→def _record_subscript_assignment(
   262→    target: ast.Subscript,
   263→    *,
   264→    lineno: int,
   265→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   266→    param_names: set[str],
   267→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   268→) -> None:
   269→    if not isinstance(target.value, ast.Name):
   270→        return
   271→    if target.value.id not in mutables or target.value.id in param_names:
   272→        return
   273→    mutations.setdefault(target.value.id, []).append(lineno)
   274→
   275→
   276→def _record_assign_mutations(
   277→    node: ast.Assign,
   278→    *,
   279→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   280→    param_names: set[str],
   281→    global_names: set[str],
   282→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   283→) -> None:
   284→    for target in node.targets:
   285→        if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
   286→            _record_name_assignment(
   287→                target,
   288→                lineno=node.lineno,
   289→                mutables=mutables,
   290→                param_names=param_names,
   291→                global_names=global_names,
   292→                mutations=mutations,
   293→            )
   294→            continue
   295→        if isinstance(target, ast.Subscript):
   296→            _record_subscript_assignment(
   297→                target,
   298→                lineno=node.lineno,
   299→                mutables=mutables,
   300→                param_names=param_names,
   301→                mutations=mutations,
   302→            )
   303→
   304→
   305→def _record_augassign_mutation(
   306→    node: ast.AugAssign,
   307→    *,
   308→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   309→    param_names: set[str],
   310→    global_names: set[str],
   311→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   312→) -> None:
   313→    if not isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
   314→        return
   315→    if node.target.id not in mutables:
   316→        return
   317→    if node.target.id in param_names or node.target.id not in global_names:
   318→        return
   319→    mutations.setdefault(node.target.id, []).append(node.lineno)
   320→
   321→
   322→def _record_call_mutation(
   323→    node: ast.Call,
   324→    *,
   325→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   326→    param_names: set[str],
   327→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   328→) -> None:
   329→    if not isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
   330→        return
   331→    if node.func.attr not in _MUTATING_METHODS:
   332→        return
   333→    if not isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name):
   334→        return
   335→    name = node.func.value.id
   336→    if name not in mutables or name in param_names:
   337→        return
   338→    mutations.setdefault(name, []).append(node.lineno)
   339→
   340→
   341→def _record_function_mutations(
   342→    node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef,
   343→    *,
   344→    mutables: dict[str, int],
   345→    param_names: set[str],
   346→    global_names: set[str],
   347→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]],
   348→) -> None:
   349→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   350→        if isinstance(child, ast.Assign):
   351→            _record_assign_mutations(
   352→                child,
   353→                mutables=mutables,
   354→                param_names=param_names,
   355→                global_names=global_names,
   356→                mutations=mutations,
   357→            )
   358→            continue
   359→        if isinstance(child, ast.AugAssign):
   360→            _record_augassign_mutation(
   361→                child,
   362→                mutables=mutables,
   363→                param_names=param_names,
   364→                global_names=global_names,
   365→                mutations=mutations,
   366→            )
   367→            continue
   368→        if isinstance(child, ast.Call):
   369→            _record_call_mutation(
   370→                child,
   371→                mutables=mutables,
   372→                param_names=param_names,
   373→                mutations=mutations,
   374→            )
   375→
   376→
   377→def _absolute_python_path(filepath: str) -> Path:
   378→    file_path = Path(filepath)
   379→    return file_path if file_path.is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   380→
   381→
   382→def _parse_python_tree(filepath: str, *, pass_name: str) -> ast.Module | None:
   383→    try:
   384→        content = _absolute_python_path(filepath).read_text()
   385→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   386→        logger.debug(
   387→            "Skipping unreadable python file %s in %s pass: %s",
   388→            filepath,
   389→            pass_name,
   390→            exc,
   391→        )
   392→        return None
   393→    try:
   394→        return ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
   395→    except SyntaxError as exc:
   396→        logger.debug(
   397→            "Skipping unparseable python file %s in %s pass: %s",
   398→            filepath,
   399→            pass_name,
   400→            exc,
   401→        )
   402→        return None
   403→
   404→
   405→def _module_paths_match(imported_module: str, source_module: str) -> bool:
   406→    return bool(
   407→        imported_module == source_module
   408→        or imported_module.endswith(f".{source_module}")
   409→        or source_module.endswith(f".{imported_module}")
   410→    )
   411→
   412→
   413→def _build_stale_import_entry(
   414→    *,
   415→    filepath: str,
   416→    module: str,
   417→    imported_name: str,
   418→    lineno: int,
   419→) -> dict:
   420→    return {
   421→        "file": filepath,
   422→        "name": imported_name,
   423→        "line": lineno,
   424→        "mutation_lines": [],
   425→        "mutation_count": 0,
   426→        "confidence": "high",
   427→        "summary": (
   428→            f"'from {module} import {imported_name}' creates stale binding — "
   429→            f"'{imported_name}' is reassigned at runtime. Import the module instead."
   430→        ),
   431→    }
   432→
   433→
   434→def _append_stale_import_entries(
   435→    filepath: str,
   436→    tree: ast.Module,
   437→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]],
   438→    entries: list[dict],
   439→) -> None:
   440→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   441→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   442→            continue
   443→        module = node.module or ""
   444→        for source_module, names in mutated_names.items():
   445→            if not _module_paths_match(module, source_module):
   446→                continue
   447→            for alias in node.names:
   448→                if alias.name in names:
   449→                    entries.append(
   450→                        _build_stale_import_entry(
   451→                            filepath=filepath,
   452→                            module=module,
   453→                            imported_name=alias.name,
   454→                            lineno=node.lineno,
   455→                        )
   456→                    )
   457→
   458→
   459→def _collect_reassigned_globals(
   460→    tree: ast.Module, mutables: dict[str, int]
   461→) -> set[str]:
   462→    reassigned: set[str] = set()
   463→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   464→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   465→            continue
   466→        for name in _function_global_names(node):
   467→            if name in mutables:
   468→                reassigned.add(name)
   469→    return reassigned
   470→
   471→
   472→def _module_path_from_file(filepath: str) -> str:
   473→    module_path = filepath.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   474→    if module_path.endswith(".py"):
   475→        module_path = module_path[:-3]
   476→    return module_path
   477→

   128→def _score_from_assessment(assessment: dict | None) -> tuple[float, float, float, bool, bool]:
   129→    has_assessment = isinstance(assessment, dict)
   130→    assessment_score = (
   131→        max(0.0, min(100.0, float(assessment.get("score", 0))))
   132→        if has_assessment
   133→        else 0.0
   134→    )
   135→    integrity_penalty = (
   136→        assessment.get("integrity_penalty")
   137→        if has_assessment
   138→        else None
   139→    )
   140→    reset_pending = bool(
   141→        has_assessment
   142→        and (
   143→            assessment.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   144→            or assessment.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   145→            or assessment.get("placeholder") is True
   146→        )
   147→    )

   149→        score = 0.0
   150→        pass_rate = 0.0
   151→    elif has_assessment:
   152→        score = assessment_score
   153→        pass_rate = score / 100.0
   154→    else:
   155→        score = 0.0
   156→        pass_rate = 0.0
   157→    return score, pass_rate, assessment_score, reset_pending, has_assessment

   160→def _component_payload(assessment: dict | None) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, float]]:

   163→    if not isinstance(assessment, dict):

   165→
   166→    raw_components = assessment.get("components")
   167→    if isinstance(raw_components, list):
   168→        components = [
   169→            str(item).strip()
   170→            for item in raw_components
   171→            if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()
   172→        ]

   174→    raw_component_scores = assessment.get("component_scores")
   175→    if isinstance(raw_component_scores, dict):
   176→        for key, value in raw_component_scores.items():
   177→            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
   178→                continue
   179→            if not is_numeric(value):
   180→                continue
   181→            component_scores[key.strip()] = round(
   182→                max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))),
   183→                1,
   184→            )

   220→    findings: dict,
   221→    assessments: dict | None,
   222→    failure_set: frozenset[str],
   223→    allowed_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   224→) -> None:
   225→    """Append subjective review dimensions to results dict (mutates results).
   226→
   227→    Subjective scoring is evidence-first: open review findings for a dimension
   228→    determine pass-rate, while imported assessment scores are retained as
   229→    metadata for transparency.
   230→    """
   231→    raw_defaults = _holistic_dimensions()
   232→    allowed = (
   233→        {_normalize_dimension_key(name) for name in allowed_dimensions}
   234→        if allowed_dimensions is not None
   235→        else None
   236→    )
   237→
   238→    default_dimensions = _normalize_default_dimensions(raw_defaults, allowed=allowed)
   239→    assessed = _normalize_assessed_dimensions(assessments, allowed=allowed)
   240→    existing_lower = {k.lower() for k in results}
   241→    lang_name = _primary_lang_from_findings(findings)
   242→
   243→    all_dims = list(default_dimensions)
   244→    for dim_name in assessed:
   245→        if dim_name not in default_dimensions:
   246→            all_dims.append(dim_name)
   247→
   248→    for dim_name in all_dims:
   249→        is_default = dim_name in default_dimensions
   250→        assessment = assessed.get(dim_name)
   251→        has_assessment = isinstance(assessment, dict)
   252→        if not is_default and not assessment:
   253→            continue
   254→
   255→        display = _dimension_display_name(dim_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   256→        if display.lower() in existing_lower:
   257→            display = f"{display} (subjective)"
   258→
   259→        issue_count = _issue_count_for_dimension(
   260→            findings,
   261→            failure_set=failure_set,
   262→            dim_name=dim_name,
   263→        )
   264→        score, pass_rate, assessment_score, reset_pending, has_assessment = (
   265→            _score_from_assessment(assessment if isinstance(assessment, dict) else None)
   266→        )
   267→        components, component_scores = _component_payload(
   268→            assessment if isinstance(assessment, dict) else None
   269→        )
   270→
   271→        results[display] = {
   272→            "score": round(float(score), 1),
   273→            "tier": 4,
   274→            "checks": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,
   275→            "issues": issue_count,
   276→            "detectors": {
   277→                "subjective_assessment": _build_subjective_detector_payload(
   278→                    pass_rate=pass_rate,
   279→                    issue_count=issue_count,
   280→                    assessment_score=assessment_score,
   281→                    reset_pending=reset_pending,
   282→                    has_assessment=has_assessment,
   283→                    dim_name=dim_name,
   284→                    lang_name=lang_name,
   285→                    components=components,
   286→                    component_scores=component_scores,
   287→                )
   288→            },
   289→        }
   290→
   291→
   292→__all__ = [
   293→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   294→    "append_subjective_dimensions",
   295→]
   296→

    11→_ROUTE_AUTH_RE = re.compile(
    12→    r"@(?:app|router|api)\.(?:get|post|put|patch|delete|route)\b"
    13→    r"|app\.(?:get|post|put|patch|delete)\("
    14→    r"|export\s+(?:async\s+)?function\s+(?:GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)\b"
    15→    r"|@router\.(?:get|post|put|patch|delete)\b",
    16→    re.MULTILINE,
    17→)
    18→_AUTH_GUARD_RE = re.compile(
    19→    r"@(?:login_required|require_auth|auth_required|requires_auth|authenticated)\b"
    20→    r"|\brequireAuth\b|\bwithAuth\b|\bgetServerSession\b|\bauthenticateRequest\b"
    21→    r"|\bauth\.getUser\b|\bsupabase\.auth\.getUser\b",
    22→)
    23→_AUTH_USAGE_RE = re.compile(r"\buseAuth\b|\brequest\.user\b|\bsession\.user\b|\bgetUser\b")
    24→_RLS_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    25→    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?(\w+)", re.IGNORECASE
    26→)
    27→_RLS_ENABLE_RE = re.compile(
    28→    r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\w+)\s+ENABLE\s+ROW\s+LEVEL\s+SECURITY"
    29→    r"|CREATE\s+POLICY\s+\w+\s+ON\s+(\w+)",
    30→    re.IGNORECASE,
    31→)

    35→class RouteAuthCoverage:
    36→    handlers: int
    37→    with_auth: int
    38→    without_auth: int
    39→
    40→    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, int]:
    41→        return {

    48→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    49→class AuthorizationSignals:
    50→    """Canonical authorization-signal payload shared by review context paths."""
    51→
    52→    route_auth_coverage: dict[str, RouteAuthCoverage] = field(default_factory=dict)
    53→    rls_with: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    54→    rls_without: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    55→    service_role_usage: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    56→    auth_patterns: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    57→    auth_guard_patterns: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    58→    auth_usage_patterns: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    59→
    60→    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
    61→        payload: dict[str, object] = {}
    62→        if self.route_auth_coverage:
    63→            payload["route_auth_coverage"] = {
    64→                path: coverage.as_dict()
    65→                for path, coverage in sorted(self.route_auth_coverage.items())
    66→            }
    67→        if self.rls_with or self.rls_without:
    68→            payload["rls_coverage"] = {
    69→                "with_rls": self.rls_with,
    70→                "without_rls": self.rls_without,
    71→            }
    72→        if self.service_role_usage:
    73→            payload["service_role_usage"] = self.service_role_usage
    74→        if self.auth_patterns:
    75→            payload["auth_patterns"] = self.auth_patterns
    76→        if self.auth_guard_patterns:
    77→            payload["auth_guard_patterns"] = self.auth_guard_patterns
    78→        if self.auth_usage_patterns:
    79→            payload["auth_usage_patterns"] = self.auth_usage_patterns
    80→        return payload
    81→
    82→
    83→def gather_auth_context(
    84→    file_contents: dict[str, str],
    85→    *,
    86→    rel_fn: Callable[[str], str],
    87→) -> dict[str, object]:
    88→    """Compute auth/RLS context from file contents.
    89→
    90→    Returns route auth coverage, RLS coverage, service role usage, and auth patterns.
    91→    """
    92→    route_auth: dict[str, RouteAuthCoverage] = {}
    93→    rls_tables: set[str] = set()
    94→    rls_enabled: set[str] = set()
    95→    service_role_files: set[str] = set()
    96→    auth_patterns: dict[str, int] = {}
    97→    auth_guard_patterns: dict[str, int] = {}
    98→    auth_usage_patterns: dict[str, int] = {}
    99→
   100→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   101→        rpath = rel_fn(filepath)
   102→
   103→        # Route auth coverage
   104→        route_segments = _route_segments(content)
   105→        if route_segments:
   106→            handler_count = len(route_segments)
   107→            auth_count = sum(1 for segment in route_segments if _AUTH_GUARD_RE.search(segment))
   108→            route_auth[rpath] = RouteAuthCoverage(
   109→                handlers=handler_count,
   110→                with_auth=auth_count,
   111→                without_auth=max(0, handler_count - auth_count),
   112→            )
   113→
   114→        # RLS coverage (SQL/migration files)
   115→        for match in _RLS_TABLE_RE.finditer(content):
   116→            rls_tables.add(match.group(1))
   117→        for match in _RLS_ENABLE_RE.finditer(content):
   118→            table = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
   119→            if table:
   120→                rls_enabled.add(table)
   121→
   122→        # Service role usage
   123→        if has_client_service_role_usage(content, filepath=filepath):
   124→            service_role_files.add(rpath)
   125→
   126→        # Auth check patterns
   127→        guard_count = len(_AUTH_GUARD_RE.findall(content))
   128→        usage_count = len(_AUTH_USAGE_RE.findall(content))
   129→        if guard_count > 0:
   130→            auth_guard_patterns[rpath] = guard_count
   131→        if usage_count > 0:
   132→            auth_usage_patterns[rpath] = usage_count
   133→        total_auth_signals = guard_count + usage_count
   134→        if total_auth_signals > 0:
   135→            auth_patterns[rpath] = total_auth_signals
   136→
   137→    return AuthorizationSignals(
   138→        route_auth_coverage=route_auth,
   139→        rls_with=sorted(rls_tables & rls_enabled),
   140→        rls_without=sorted(rls_tables - rls_enabled),
   141→        service_role_usage=sorted(service_role_files),
   142→        auth_patterns=auth_patterns,
   143→        auth_guard_patterns=auth_guard_patterns,
   144→        auth_usage_patterns=auth_usage_patterns,
   145→    ).as_dict()
   146→
   147→
   148→def _route_segments(content: str) -> list[str]:
   149→    """Split source into route-handler scoped segments."""
   150→    matches = list(_ROUTE_AUTH_RE.finditer(content))
   151→    if not matches:
   152→        return []
   153→    segments: list[str] = []
   154→    for idx, match in enumerate(matches):
   155→        start = match.start()
   156→        end = matches[idx + 1].start() if idx + 1 < len(matches) else len(content)
   157→        segments.append(content[start:end])
   158→    return segments
   159→
   160→
   161→__all__ = ["AuthorizationSignals", "RouteAuthCoverage", "gather_auth_context"]
   162→

     2→

    13→from desloppify.core.text_api import is_numeric
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import _matches_pattern
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import (
    16→    StateModel,
    17→    ensure_state_defaults,
    18→    utc_now,
    19→    validate_state_invariants,
    20→)
    21→from desloppify.engine._state.scoring import _recompute_stats
    22→
    23→
    24→def coerce_assessment_score(value: object) -> float | None:
    25→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float.
    26→
    27→    Returns ``None`` when the value cannot be interpreted as a numeric score
    28→    (e.g. bools, non-numeric strings, missing keys).
    29→    """
    30→    if is_numeric(value):
    31→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))), 1)
    32→    if isinstance(value, dict):
    33→        raw = value.get("score")
    34→        if not is_numeric(raw):
    35→            return None
    36→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(raw))), 1)
    37→    return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
    41→    state: StateModel,
    42→    *,
    43→    status: str,
    44→    resolved_findings: list[dict],
    45→    now: str,
    46→) -> None:
    47→    """Mark subjective assessments as stale when review findings are resolved.
    48→
    49→    The assessment score is preserved (not zeroed) — only a fresh review import
    50→    should change dimension scores.  The stale marker tells the UI to prompt
    51→    for a re-review.
    52→    """
    53→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    54→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    55→        return
    56→
    57→    touched_dimensions: set[str] = set()
    58→    for finding in resolved_findings:
    59→        if finding.get("detector") != "review":
    60→            continue
    61→        dimension = str(finding.get("detail", {}).get("dimension", "")).strip()
    62→        if dimension:
    63→            touched_dimensions.add(dimension)
    64→
    65→    for dimension in sorted(touched_dimensions):
    66→        if dimension not in assessments:
    67→            continue
    68→
    69→        payload = assessments.get(dimension)
    70→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
    71→            payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    72→            payload["refresh_reason"] = f"review_finding_{status}"
    73→            payload["stale_since"] = now
    74→        else:
    75→            assessments[dimension] = {
    76→                "score": coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0,
    77→                "needs_review_refresh": True,
    78→                "refresh_reason": f"review_finding_{status}",
    79→                "stale_since": now,
    80→            }
    81→
    82→
    83→def match_findings(
    84→    state: StateModel, pattern: str, status_filter: str = "open"
    85→) -> list[dict]:
    86→    """Return findings matching *pattern* with the given status."""
    87→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
    88→    return [
    89→        finding
    90→        for finding_id, finding in state["findings"].items()
    91→        if not finding.get("suppressed")
    92→        if (status_filter == "all" or finding["status"] == status_filter)
    93→        and _matches_pattern(finding_id, finding, pattern)
    94→    ]
    95→
    96→
    97→def resolve_findings(
    98→    state: StateModel,
    99→    pattern: str,
   100→    status: str,
   101→    note: str | None = None,
   102→    attestation: str | None = None,
   103→) -> list[str]:
   104→    """Set finding status for matches and return affected finding IDs."""
   105→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   106→    now = utc_now()
   107→    resolved: list[str] = []
   108→    resolved_findings: list[dict] = []
   109→    status_filter = "all" if status == "open" else "open"
   110→    for finding in match_findings(state, pattern, status_filter=status_filter):
   111→        previous_status = str(finding.get("status", "open")).strip() or "open"
   112→        if status == "open" and previous_status == "open":
   113→            continue
   114→
   115→        extra_updates: dict[str, object] = {}
   116→        if status == "wontfix":
   117→            snapshot_scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   118→            extra_updates["wontfix_scan_count"] = snapshot_scan_count
   119→            extra_updates["wontfix_snapshot"] = {
   120→                "captured_at": now,
   121→                "scan_count": snapshot_scan_count,
   122→                "tier": finding.get("tier"),
   123→                "confidence": finding.get("confidence"),
   124→                "detail": copy.deepcopy(finding.get("detail", {})),
   125→            }
   126→        if status == "open":
   127→            finding["reopen_count"] = int(finding.get("reopen_count", 0) or 0) + 1
   128→            finding.pop("wontfix_scan_count", None)
   129→            finding.pop("wontfix_snapshot", None)
   130→            previous_note = finding.get("note")
   131→            next_note = note if note is not None else previous_note
   132→            extra_updates["resolved_at"] = None
   133→            extra_updates["note"] = next_note
   134→            extra_updates["resolution_attestation"] = {
   135→                "kind": "manual_reopen",
   136→                "text": attestation or note,
   137→                "attested_at": now,
   138→                "scan_verified": False,
   139→            }
   140→            extra_updates["resolution_attestation"]["previous_status"] = previous_status
   141→
   142→        updates: dict[str, object] = {
   143→            "status": status,
   144→            "note": note,
   145→            "resolved_at": now,
   146→            "suppressed": False,
   147→            "suppressed_at": None,
   148→            "suppression_pattern": None,
   149→            "resolution_attestation": {
   150→                "kind": "manual",
   151→                "text": attestation,
   152→                "attested_at": now,
   153→                "scan_verified": False,
   154→            },
   155→        }
   156→        updates.update(extra_updates)
   157→        finding.update(updates)
   158→        resolved.append(finding["id"])
   159→        resolved_findings.append(finding)
   160→
   161→    _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
   162→        state,
   163→        status=status,
   164→        resolved_findings=resolved_findings,
   165→        now=now,
   166→    )
   167→
   168→    _recompute_stats(state, scan_path=state.get("scan_path"))
   169→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   170→    return resolved
   171→
