   113→def _collect_reviewed_files_from_batches(
   114→    *,
   115→    batches: list[dict[str, object]],
   116→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   117→) -> list[str]:
   118→    """Collect normalized file paths reviewed in the selected batch set."""
   119→    reviewed: list[str] = []
   120→    seen: set[str] = set()
   121→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   122→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(batches):
   123→            continue
   124→        batch = batches[idx]
   125→        files = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   126→        if not isinstance(files, list):
   127→            continue
   128→        for raw in files:
   129→            if not isinstance(raw, str):
   130→                continue
   131→            path = raw.strip().strip(",'\"")
   132→            if not path or path in {".", ".."}:
   133→                continue
   134→            if path.endswith("/"):
   135→                continue
   136→            if path in seen:
   137→                continue
   138→            seen.add(path)
   139→            reviewed.append(path)
   140→    return reviewed
   141→
   142→
   143→def _normalize_dimension_list(raw: object) -> list[str]:
   144→    """Normalize dimension collections to a stable, de-duplicated list."""
   145→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
   146→        return []
   147→    out: list[str] = []
   148→    seen: set[str] = set()
   149→    for item in raw:
   150→        if not isinstance(item, str):
   151→            continue
   152→        dim = item.strip()
   153→        if not dim or dim in seen:
   154→            continue
   155→        seen.add(dim)
   156→        out.append(dim)
   157→    return out
   158→
   159→
   160→def _scored_dimensions_for_lang(
   161→    lang_name: str,
   162→    *,
   163→    warning_sink: list[NonFatalIssue] | None = None,
   164→) -> list[str]:
   165→    """Return default scored subjective dimensions for one language."""
   166→    try:
   167→        default_dims, _, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   168→    except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   169→        report_non_fatal_issue(
   170→            NonFatalIssue(
   171→                operation="review.batches.load_dimensions_for_lang",
   172→                target=lang_name,
   173→                error_type=type(exc).__name__,
   174→                message=str(exc),
   175→            ),
   176→            sink=warning_sink,
   177→        )
   178→        return []
   179→    return _normalize_dimension_list(default_dims)
   180→
   181→
   182→def _missing_scored_dimensions(
   183→    *,
   184→    selected_dims: list[str],
   185→    scored_dims: list[str],
   186→) -> list[str]:
   187→    selected = set(selected_dims)
   188→    return [dim for dim in scored_dims if dim not in selected]
   189→
   190→
   191→def _missing_dimensions_command(*, missing_dims: list[str], scan_path: str) -> str:
   192→    """Return rerun command for missing subjective dimensions."""
   193→    base = "desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import"
   194→    if scan_path and scan_path != ".":
   195→        base += f" --path {shlex.quote(scan_path)}"
   196→    if missing_dims:
   197→        base += f" --dimensions {','.join(missing_dims)}"
   198→    return base

   315→
   316→
   317→def _write_live_snapshot(state: _RunnerState, ctx: _AttemptContext) -> None:
   318→    """Write a point-in-time log snapshot while the runner is active."""
   319→    elapsed_seconds = int(max(0.0, time.monotonic() - ctx.started_monotonic))
   320→    with state.lock:
   321→        stdout_preview = "".join(state.stdout_chunks)
   322→        stderr_preview = "".join(state.stderr_chunks)
   323→        note = state.runner_note
   324→    note_block = f"\nRUNNER NOTE: {note}" if note else ""
   325→    ctx.safe_write_text_fn(
   326→        ctx.log_file,
   327→        "\n\n".join(
   328→            ctx.log_sections
   329→            + [
   330→                (
   331→                    f"{ctx.header}\n\n"
   332→                    "STATUS: running\n"
   333→                    f"STARTED AT: {ctx.started_at_iso}\n"
   334→                    f"ELAPSED: {elapsed_seconds}s\n"
   335→                    f"OUTPUT FILE: {_output_file_status_text(ctx.output_file)}"
   336→                    f"{note_block}\n\n"
   337→                    f"STDOUT (live):\n{stdout_preview}\n\n"
   338→                    f"STDERR (live):\n{stderr_preview}\n"
   339→                )
   340→            ]
   341→        ),
   342→    )
   343→
   344→
   345→def _start_live_writer(
   346→    state: _RunnerState, ctx: _AttemptContext, interval: float,
   347→) -> threading.Thread:
   348→    """Spawn a daemon thread that periodically writes live log snapshots."""
   349→    def _loop() -> None:
   350→        while not state.stop_event.wait(interval):
   351→            _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   352→
   353→    thread = threading.Thread(target=_loop, daemon=True)
   354→    thread.start()
   355→    return thread
   356→
   357→
   358→def _check_stall(
   359→    output_file: Path,
   360→    prev_sig: tuple[int, int] | None,
   361→    prev_stable: float | None,
   362→    now: float,
   363→    last_activity: float,
   364→    threshold: int,
   365→) -> tuple[bool, tuple[int, int] | None, float | None]:
   366→    """Check for runner stall. Returns (stalled, new_sig, new_stable_since)."""
   367→    try:
   368→        stat = output_file.stat()
   369→        current_signature: tuple[int, int] | None = (int(stat.st_size), int(stat.st_mtime))
   370→    except OSError:
   371→        current_signature = None
   372→    if current_signature is None:
   373→        # If no output file ever appears, still recover from a silent hang once
   374→        # both output state and process streams have been idle long enough.
   375→        baseline = (
   376→            prev_stable if isinstance(prev_stable, int | float) else now
   377→        )
   378→        output_age = now - baseline
   379→        stream_idle = now - last_activity
   380→        if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
   381→            return True, None, baseline
   382→        return False, None, baseline
   383→    if current_signature != prev_sig:
   384→        return False, current_signature, now
   385→    if prev_stable is None:
   386→        return False, prev_sig, prev_stable
   387→    output_age = now - prev_stable
   388→    stream_idle = now - last_activity
   389→    if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
   390→        return True, prev_sig, prev_stable
   391→    return False, prev_sig, prev_stable
   392→
   393→
   394→def _run_via_popen(
   395→    cmd: list[str],
   396→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   397→    state: _RunnerState,
   398→    ctx: _AttemptContext,
   399→    interval: float,
   400→    stall_seconds: int,
   401→) -> _ExecutionResult:
   402→    """Execute batch via Popen with live streaming and stall recovery."""
   403→    writer_thread = _start_live_writer(state, ctx, interval)
   404→    try:
   405→        process = deps.subprocess_popen(
   406→            cmd,
   407→            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
   408→            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
   409→            text=True,
   410→            bufsize=1,
   411→        )
   412→    except OSError as exc:
   413→        state.stop_event.set()
   414→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   415→        ctx.log_sections.append(f"{ctx.header}\n\nRUNNER ERROR:\n{exc}\n")
   416→        ctx.safe_write_text_fn(ctx.log_file, "\n\n".join(ctx.log_sections))
   417→        return _ExecutionResult(code=127, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=127)
   418→    except (
   419→        RuntimeError,
   420→        ValueError,
   421→        TypeError,
   422→        subprocess.SubprocessError,
   423→    ) as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive boundary
   424→        state.stop_event.set()
   425→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   426→        ctx.log_sections.append(f"{ctx.header}\n\nUNEXPECTED RUNNER ERROR:\n{exc}\n")
   427→        ctx.safe_write_text_fn(ctx.log_file, "\n\n".join(ctx.log_sections))
   428→        return _ExecutionResult(code=1, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=1)
   429→
   430→    stdout_thread = threading.Thread(
   431→        target=_drain_stream,
   432→        args=(process.stdout, state.stdout_chunks, state),
   433→        daemon=True,
   434→    )
   435→    stderr_thread = threading.Thread(
   436→        target=_drain_stream,
   437→        args=(process.stderr, state.stderr_chunks, state),
   438→        daemon=True,
   439→    )
   440→    stdout_thread.start()
   441→    stderr_thread.start()
   442→
   443→    timed_out = False
   444→    stalled = False
   445→    recovered_from_stall = False
   446→    output_signature: tuple[int, int] | None = None
   447→    output_stable_since: float | None = None
   448→
   449→    while process.poll() is None:
   450→        now_monotonic = time.monotonic()
   451→        elapsed = int(max(0.0, now_monotonic - ctx.started_monotonic))
   452→        if elapsed >= deps.timeout_seconds:
   453→            with state.lock:
   454→                state.runner_note = f"timeout after {deps.timeout_seconds}s"
   455→            timed_out = True
   456→            _terminate_process(process)
   457→            break
   458→        if stall_seconds > 0:
   459→            with state.lock:
   460→                last_activity = state.last_stream_activity
   461→            stalled, output_signature, output_stable_since = _check_stall(
   462→                ctx.output_file,
   463→                output_signature,
   464→                output_stable_since,
   465→                now_monotonic,
   466→                last_activity,
   467→                stall_seconds,
   468→            )
   469→            if stalled:
   470→                stalled = True
   471→                with state.lock:
   472→                    state.runner_note = (
   473→                        f"stall recovery triggered after {stall_seconds}s "
   474→                        "with stable output state"
   475→                    )
   476→                recovered_from_stall = _output_file_has_json_payload(ctx.output_file)
   477→                _terminate_process(process)
   478→                break
   479→        deps.sleep_fn(min(interval, 1.0))
   480→
   481→    if process.poll() is None:
   482→        _terminate_process(process)
   483→    stdout_thread.join(timeout=2)
   484→    stderr_thread.join(timeout=2)
   485→    state.stop_event.set()
   486→    writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   487→    _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   488→
   489→    return _ExecutionResult(
   490→        code=int(process.returncode or 0),
   491→        stdout_text="".join(state.stdout_chunks),
   492→        stderr_text="".join(state.stderr_chunks),
   493→        timed_out=timed_out,
   494→        stalled=stalled,
   495→        recovered_from_stall=recovered_from_stall,
   496→    )
   497→

   499→def _run_via_subprocess(
   500→    cmd: list[str],
   501→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   502→    state: _RunnerState,

   504→    interval: float,

   506→    """Execute batch via subprocess.run (compatibility path for tests)."""
   507→    writer_thread = _start_live_writer(state, ctx, interval)

   528→        return _ExecutionResult(code=127, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=127)

   530→        state.stop_event.set()

## Comprehensive Plan Infrastructure Report

I've thoroughly explored the desloppify plan infrastructure. Here's the complete breakdown:

---

### 1. **Plan Data Model** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py`)

The plan is a versioned JSON document with these TypedDict structures:

```python
PlanModel:
  - version: Required[int]  # PLAN_VERSION = 2
  - created: Required[str]  # ISO timestamp
  - updated: Required[str]  # ISO timestamp
  - queue_order: list[str]  # Ordered finding IDs
  - deferred: list[str]  # DEPRECATED (v1→v2 migration), kept empty
  - skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry]  # Deferred work items
  - active_cluster: str | None  # User focus
  - overrides: dict[str, ItemOverride]  # Per-finding annotations
  - clusters: dict[str, Cluster]  # User & auto-generated clusters
  - superseded: dict[str, SupersededEntry]  # Tracking disappeared findings
  - queue_sync_markers: dict[str, int]  # Subjective injection cadence

SkipEntry:  # A suppressed/deferred finding
  - finding_id: Required[str]
  - kind: Required[str]  # "temporary" | "permanent" | "false_positive"
  - reason: str | None
  - note: str | None  # wontfix note for permanent
  - attestation: str | None  # required for permanent/false_positive
  - created_at: str
  - review_after: int | None  # scans until resurfaced (temp only)
  - skipped_at_scan: int

ItemOverride:  # Per-finding metadata
  - finding_id: Required[str]
  - description: str | None
  - note: str | None
  - cluster: str | None
  - created_at: str
  - updated_at: str

Cluster:  # Grouped findings (auto or manual)
  - name: Required[str]
  - description: str | None
  - finding_ids: list[str]
  - created_at: str
  - updated_at: str
  - auto: bool  # True for auto-generated
  - cluster_key: str  # Deterministic grouping key
  - action: str | None  # Primary resolution command/guidance
  - user_modified: bool  # True when user edits auto-cluster membership

SupersededEntry:  # Tracking missing findings
  - original_id: Required[str]
  - original_detector: str
  - original_file: str
  - original_summary: str
  - status: str  # "superseded" | "remapped" | "dismissed"
  - superseded_at: str
  - remapped_to: str | None
  - candidates: list[str]  # up to 5 similar findings
  - note: str | None
```

**Key invariants**:
- No finding ID can appear in both `queue_order` and `skipped`
- `skip_kind` must be in `{"temporary", "permanent", "false_positive"}`
- Validates on load/save

---

### 2. **Auto-Clustering Algorithm** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py`)

**Main entry point**: `auto_cluster_findings(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> int`

**Grouping key computation**:
- **Review/Subjective**: `review::<dimension>` (groups by dimension name)
- **File-scoped**: `file::<detector>::<normalized_path>` (for structural/responsibility_cohesion)
- **Typed/subtypes**: `typed::<detector>::<subtype>` (for detectors with subtypes like `dict_keys::phantom_read`)
- **Auto-fix detectors**: `auto::<detector>` (pure auto-fix, no subtypes)
- **Fallback**: `detector::<detector>`

**Cluster naming**: Converts grouping keys to `auto/` prefixed names:
- `auto::unused` → `auto/unused`
- `typed::dict_keys::phantom_read` → `auto/dict_keys-phantom_read`
- `file::structural::big_file.py` → `auto/structural-big_file__py`
- `review::abstraction_fitness` → `auto/review-abstraction_fitness`

**Description & action generation**:
- Generates human-readable descriptions from detector metadata (e.g., "Fix 5 unused imports")
- Action templates based on `meta.action_type`: reorganize, refactor, manual_fix
- Extracts fixer command from subtype (e.g., `desloppify fix unused-imports --dry-run`)
- Has fallback guidance from detector registry

**Algorithm steps**:
1. Groups all open, non-suppressed findings by their grouping key
2. Filters to groups with ≥2 members (minimum cluster size)
3. Manages manual vs auto clusters separately
4. Upserts/updates clusters, preserving user-modified markers
5. Handles subjective dimensions specially (stale/unscored clusters)
6. Deletes stale auto-clusters with no alive members
7. Preserves user-modified auto-clusters even if key changes

**Returns**: Count of changes made

---

### 3. **Reconciliation** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/reconcile.py`)

**Main entry point**: `reconcile_plan_after_scan(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> ReconcileResult`

**What it does** (runs after every scan):
1. Collects all finding IDs referenced in the plan (queue_order, skipped, overrides, cluster members)
2. **Supersedes** IDs that no longer exist or are closed
   - Moves them to `superseded` dict with context (original detector, file, summary)
   - Finds candidate remapped findings
   - Clears cluster refs, removes from queue_order/skipped
3. **Resurfaces** temporary skips past their `review_after` threshold (calls `resurface_stale_skips`)
4. **Prunes** old superseded entries (90-day TTL by default)

**Result dataclass**:
```python
ReconcileResult:
  - superseded: list[str]  # IDs moved to superseded
  - pruned: list[str]  # TTL-expired IDs removed
  - resurfaced: list[str]  # Temporary skips brought back
  - changes: int  # Total mutations
```

**Trigger point**: `_reconcile_plan_best_effort()` in `scan_workflow.py` (line 487-517)

---

### 4. **Plan Operations** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/operations.py`)

**Queue management**:
- `move_items(plan, finding_ids, position, target=None, offset=None) -> int`
  - Positions: `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"before"`, `"after"`, `"up"`, `"down"`
  - Returns count moved
- `skip_items(plan, finding_ids, *, options=SkipItemsOptions) -> int`
  - Creates SkipEntry with kind/reason/note/attestation
  - Returns count skipped
- `unskip_items(plan, finding_ids) -> tuple[int, list[str]]`
  - Returns (count_unskipped, IDs_needing_state_reopen)
  - For permanent/false_positive skips, caller must reopen their state status
- `resurface_stale_skips(plan, current_scan_count) -> list[str]`
  - Auto-resurfacing of temporary skips past review_after threshold

**Annotation**:
- `describe_finding(plan, finding_id, description: str | None)` — augment display text
- `annotate_finding(plan, finding_id, note: str | None)` — add private note

**Cluster management**:
- `create_cluster(plan, name, description=None, action=None) -> Cluster`
  - Raises if name starts with `"auto/"` (reserved for auto-clusters)
- `add_to_cluster(plan, cluster_name, finding_ids) -> int`
  - Updates overrides to track membership
- `remove_from_cluster(plan, cluster_name, finding_ids) -> int`
  - Marks auto-clusters as `user_modified` when items removed
- `delete_cluster(plan, name) -> list[str]`
  - Returns orphaned IDs (not removed from queue)
- `move_cluster(plan, cluster_name, position, ...) -> int`
  - Moves all cluster members as contiguous block

**Focus**:
- `set_focus(plan, cluster_name)` — sets `active_cluster`
- `clear_focus(plan)` — clears focus

**Administrative**:
- `reset_plan(plan)` — resets to empty, preserving version/created timestamp
- `purge_ids(plan, finding_ids) -> int`
  - Removes from queue_order, skipped, and all cluster memberships
  - Preserves overrides (descriptions/notes) for history

---

### 5. **Persistence** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/persistence.py`)

**File location**: `.desloppify/plan.json` (derived from state dir via `get_state_dir()`)

**Functions**:
- `get_plan_file() -> Path` — returns current plan.json path
- `load_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> PlanModel`
  - Returns empty plan on missing/corrupted files
  - Handles JSON decode errors, validates invariants
  - Applies migrations (v1→v2 deferred→skipped)
  - Warns on version mismatch
- `save_plan(plan: PlanModel | dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None`
  - Validates invariants before save
  - Updates `updated` timestamp
  - Creates `.json.bak` backup before atomic write
  - Uses `safe_write_text()` for atomic writes
- `has_living_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> bool`
  - True if plan.json exists and has user intent (queue_order, overrides, or clusters)
- `plan_path_for_state(state_path: Path) -> Path`
  - Derives plan.json location from state file path

**Atomic write protocol**: Backup → write to temp → atomic rename

---

### 6. **Scan Workflow Integration** (`desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_workflow.py`)

**Main reconciliation trigger**: `_reconcile_plan_best_effort()` (lines 487-517)

Called from `merge_scan_results()` at line 475, after state is saved.

**Steps**:
1. Loads plan from disk (best-effort, doesn't fail scan)
2. `_reconcile_existing_plan()` — if plan has content, calls `reconcile_plan_after_scan()`
3. `_sync_unscored_dimensions()` — injects unscored placeholder dimensions
4. `_sync_stale_dimension_queue()` — injects stale dimensions
5. `auto_cluster_findings()` — regenerates auto-clusters
6. Saves if any changes made (`dirty` flag)

**Error handling**: Wrapped in try/except for `_PLAN_SYNC_EXCEPTIONS` and `_PLAN_SYNC_UNEXPECTED_EXCEPTIONS`:
- Sets `state.plan_sync_failed = True`
- Logs warnings
- Records scan warning but doesn't fail the scan
- Prints user-facing colorized status updates

**Status messages printed**:
```
Plan: N skipped item(s) re-surfaced after review period.
Plan: N unscored subjective dimension(s) queued for initial review.
Plan: N refreshed subjective dimension(s) removed from queue.
Plan: N stale subjective dimension(s) queued for refresh.
```

---

### 7. **Subjective Dimension Syncing** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py`)

Two independent sync functions with bounded interleaving to prevent queue inversion:

**`sync_unscored_dimensions(plan, state) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult`**
- **Prune**: Removes subjective IDs no longer unscored (unless stale)
- **Inject**: Front-injects unscored dims when objective backlog ≤40 items
  - Otherwise interleaves 2 per scan at position 12, every 2 scans
- Uses marker `queue_sync_markers["last_unscored_injected_scan"]` to track cadence
- Constants:
  - `_UNSCORED_FRONT_INJECT_OBJECTIVE_MAX = 40`
  - `_UNSCORED_MAX_PER_SCAN = 2`
  - `_UNSCORED_INTERLEAVE_EVERY_SCANS = 2`
  - `_UNSCORED_INTERLEAVE_INDEX = 12`

**`sync_stale_dimensions(plan, state) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult`**
- **Prune**: Removes subjective IDs no longer stale (unless unscored)
- **Inject**: Appends all stale IDs when objective queue empty
  - Otherwise interleaves 2 per scan at position 24, every 3 scans
- Uses marker `queue_sync_markers["last_stale_injected_scan"]`
- Constants:
  - `_STALE_MAX_PER_SCAN = 2`
  - `_STALE_INTERLEAVE_EVERY_SCANS = 3`
  - `_STALE_INTERLEAVE_INDEX = 24`

**Subjective ID format**: `subjective::<slugified_dimension_key>`
- Example: `subjective::abstraction_fitness`

---

### 8. **Public API Facade** (`desloppify/engine/plan.py`)

All the above modules are re-exported via a single facade for clean imports:

```python
# schema
PlanModel, Cluster, ItemOverride, SkipEntry, SupersededEntry
PLAN_VERSION, VALID_SKIP_KINDS
empty_plan, ensure_plan_defaults, validate_plan

# persistence
PLAN_FILE, get_plan_file, load_plan, save_plan, plan_path_for_state, has_living_plan

# operations
move_items, skip_items, unskip_items, resurface_stale_skips
describe_finding, annotate_finding
create_cluster, add_to_cluster, remove_from_cluster, delete_cluster, move_cluster
set_focus, clear_focus
reset_plan, purge_ids

# reconcile
ReconcileResult, reconcile_plan_after_scan

# auto-clustering
AUTO_PREFIX, auto_cluster_findings

# stale dimensions
UnscoredDimensionSyncResult, StaleDimensionSyncResult
sync_unscored_dimensions, sync_stale_dimensions
```

---

### Key Architecture Insights

1. **No traditional "epics"**: Plan uses **clusters** as the grouping concept
   - Auto-clusters are deterministically regenerated from detector/subtype/file patterns
   - Manual clusters are user-created and preserved
   - User modifications to auto-clusters are tracked to prevent data loss

2. **Living plan concept**: Plan is "alive" if it has `queue_order`, `overrides`, `clusters`, or `skipped` content
   - Reconciliation only runs on living plans
   - Supports plan-aware CLI surfaces (next, status, show, scan LLM block)

3. **Subjective dimensions are synthetic findings**: Stored as `subjective::<slug>` IDs in queue
   - Front-injected for initial scoring
   - Stale ones interleaved on bounded cadence to prevent starvation
   - Managed separately from objective findings

4. **Superseded entries track context**: When findings disappear, the plan records
   - Original detector/file/summary for audit trail
   - Up to 5 candidate replacement findings
   - User notes are preserved
   - 90-day TTL before cleanup

5. **Atomic writes with backup**: All plan saves are atomic with `.json.bak` backups
   - Corruption handling returns empty plan gracefully
   - Validation happens on load and save

6. **Scan integration is best-effort**: Plan reconciliation errors don't fail the scan
   - Errors logged, state marked with `plan_sync_failed` flag
   - User sees colored status messages

---

This is the complete infrastructure. The plan is a sophisticated living document that manages both objective findings and subjective dimensions, with smart clustering, skip tracking, and bounded interleaving to prevent queue inversion.

## Complete Flow Report: Review Import to State Update

I've thoroughly explored the review import and subjective assessment flow in desloppify. Here's the complete end-to-end process from "review results arrive" to "state is updated with findings and assessments":

---

### **HIGH-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE**

The review import system has three main entry points:
1. **Holistic imports** - codebase-wide review findings via `import_holistic_findings()`
2. **Per-file imports** - targeted per-file review findings via `import_review_findings()`
3. **Batch mode** - agent-driven batch processing via `review --run-batches --runner codex`

All paths converge on the same state mutation mechanism.

---

### **1. ENTRY POINT: `do_import()` in import_cmd.py (lines 557-604)**

This is the main CLI handler when users run `desloppify review --import <file>`.

**Key steps:**
- Normalizes CLI flags into `_ImportCommandFlags` 
- Builds an immutable `ReviewImportOptions` request object
- Loads and validates the import payload from file
- Runs import preflight checks
- Executes the import transaction
- Persists state atomically
- Renders summary and writes query metadata

**Flag processing:**
- `--allow-partial` - Skip validation guard for partial imports
- `--trusted-assessment-source` - Mark assessments as trusted internal
- `--attested-external` / `--attest` - Require signed external provenance + attestation
- `--manual-override` / `--attest` - Manual user-attested override (provisional)
- `--assessment-override` / `--assessment-note` - Legacy aliases

---

### **2. PAYLOAD VALIDATION: import_helpers.py**

The import payload must conform to `ReviewImportPayload` (contracts.py lines 270-279):

```python
ReviewImportPayload = {
    "findings": list[ReviewFindingPayload],      # Required
    "assessments": dict[str, Any],               # Required (can be empty)
    "reviewed_files": list[str],                 # Required (can be empty)
    "review_scope": ReviewScopePayload,          # Optional metadata
    "provenance": ReviewProvenancePayload,       # Optional trust metadata
    "dimension_notes": dict[str, Any],           # Optional
    "_assessment_policy": AssessmentImportPolicy # Internal
}
```

**Finding validation** (`contracts.py` lines 214-250):
- Each finding must have: `dimension`, `identifier`, `summary`, `confidence` (high/medium/low), `suggestion`, `related_files`, `evidence`
- Optional: `file`, `reasoning`, `evidence_lines`, `concern_verdict`, `concern_fingerprint`, `concern_type`, `concern_file`
- **Dismissed findings** are special: marked with `concern_verdict: "dismissed"` and store fingerprints for suppression

**Assessment policy determination** (import_helpers.py lines 594+):
Four modes with increasing trust:
1. **"none"** - No assessments in payload, findings-only import
2. **"trusted_internal"** - From internal blind batch (`--run-batches --runner codex`)
3. **"attested_external"** - External runner (Claude) with signature + blind packet proof + manual attestation
4. **"manual_override"** - User-attested override (provisional, expires next scan)

### **3. FINDINGS IMPORT: shared.py and holistic.py/per_file.py**

#### **Holistic Import** (`import_holistic_findings()` in holistic.py lines 336-462)

**Preprocessing:**
1. Parses payload via `parse_review_import_payload()` → `ReviewImportEnvelope`
2. Stores assessments in `state["subjective_assessments"]` via `store_assessments()` (source="holistic")
3. Loads dimension prompts for language
4. Validates each finding payload and builds state-ready finding dicts

**Finding construction** (`_build_imported_finding()` lines 116-151):
- Creates stable ID: `{detector}::{file}::{name}` where name includes dimension, identifier, content hash
- Detector is "concerns" for confirmed verdicts, "review" for regular findings
- Tier derived from confidence + scope (high/holistic → tier 1, medium → tier 2, low → tier 3)
- Detail includes: holistic flag, dimension, related_files, evidence, suggestion, reasoning
- Marks with `lang=lang_name`

**State mutation via `merge_scan()`** (lines 412-420):
- Calls `merge_scan(state, review_findings, MergeScanOptions(potentials={...}, merge_potentials=True))`
- This inserts findings and tracks diff (new, reopened counts)
- Returns `diff` dict with counts

**Dismissed concerns** (lines 381-398):
- Dismissed findings store fingerprints in `state["concern_dismissals"]`
- Links to source finding IDs via concern generation
- Used later to suppress concern generation

**Auto-resolution** (`_auto_resolve_stale_holistic()` lines 295-333):
- Existing open "review"/"concerns" findings NOT in latest import are auto-resolved
- Respects import scope: full sweep vs. scoped re-import
- Tracks resolved count in diff

**Scope update** (lines 436-455):
- Updates `state["review_cache"]["holistic"]` with review metadata
- Stores total file count, finding count, reviewed file count, full sweep flag
- Handles coverage markers: resolves `subjective_review` findings for unreviewed/stale coverage
- Updates per-file cache entries for reviewed files

#### **Per-File Import** (`import_review_findings()` in per_file.py lines 54-196)

Similar flow but file-scoped:
- Each finding requires `file`, `dimension`, `identifier`, `summary`, `confidence`
- Absolutizes paths to resolve them canonically
- Only auto-resolves findings in the reimported file set
- Updates `state["review_cache"]["files"][file_path]` with content hash, review timestamp, finding count

### **5. FINDINGS MERGE LOGIC: engine/_state/merge_findings.py**

#### **upsert_findings()** (lines 214-274):
Inserts new findings and updates existing ones:
1. **New findings**: Added to state with timestamp, unchecked
2. **Existing findings**: Fields updated (last_seen, tier, confidence, summary, detail, zone, lang)
3. **Ignored findings**: Suppressed by ignore patterns
4. **Reopenable findings**: Fixed/auto_resolved findings that reappear are reopened with reopen_count++
5. Returns: (current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, by_detector, ignored_count, changed_detectors)

#### **auto_resolve_disappeared()** (lines 171-211):
Auto-resolves open findings NOT in the fresh scan:
- Skips findings from suspect detectors (didn't actually run or import-only like "review")
- Skips if language mismatch or out of scan scope
- Marks as `auto_resolved` with `resolution_attestation={kind: "scan_verified", ...}`
- Returns: (resolved_count, skipped_other_lang, skipped_out_of_scope, resolved_detectors)

#### **find_suspect_detectors()** (lines 131-168):
Detects detectors that likely didn't run:
- "review" always suspect (import-only)
- Detectors with ≥3 open findings but 0 current findings
- Except when explicitly in `ran_detectors` set

### **6. MERGE TRANSACTION: engine/_state/merge.py**

#### **merge_scan()** (lines 108-123):
Main entry point that orchestrates the merge:
```
1. ensure_state_defaults(state)
2. _record_scan_metadata() - Update scan timestamps
3. _merge_scan_inputs() - Merge potentials if requested
4. upsert_findings() - Add/update findings
5. find_suspect_detectors() - Identify non-runners
6. auto_resolve_disappeared() - Resolve missing findings
7. _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change() - Mark subjective stale
8. _recompute_stats() - Recalculate counts/scores
9. _append_scan_history() - Log scan
10. Build diff and return
```

#### **Subjective staleness marking** (lines 55-89):
When mechanical findings change (upsert or resolve):
- Maps changed detectors → affected subjective dimensions
- Marks assessments stale ONLY if already have an assessment
- Doesn't create new entries
- Example: `structural` detector → `{design_coherence, abstraction_fitness}`

### **7. ASSESSMENT STORAGE & POLICY**

#### **store_assessments()** (shared.py lines 103-139):
Stores dimension scores in `state["subjective_assessments"]`:
- Dimension key normalized via `normalize_dimension_name()`
- Score clamped to 0-100
- Holistic assessments overwrite per-file for same dimension
- Per-file doesn't overwrite holistic
- Records source ("per_file" or "holistic"), timestamp
- Stores optional components and component_scores

#### **Policy effects** (import_cmd.py lines 349-367):
After findings import, policy dictates metadata updates:
- **manual_override**: Marks assessments `provisional_override=True`, `provisional_until_scan=scan_count+1`, `source="manual_override"`
- **trusted_internal/attested_external**: Clears provisional flags if present, updates source

### **8. SUBJECTIVE SCORING: engine/_scoring/subjective/core.py**

#### **append_subjective_dimensions()** (lines 218-289):
Computes subjective dimension scores for scoring output:

**Evidence-first approach:**
1. Looks at open "review"/"concerns" findings for the dimension
2. Issue count = evidence for **pass-rate** calculation
3. Pass-rate = (SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS - issues) / SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS
4. Assessment score (if present) stored as metadata only

**Score computation** (`_score_from_assessment()` lines 128-157):
- If assessment dict exists: score = clamp(assessment["score"], 0, 100)
- Pass-rate = score / 100
- Special: resets if `placeholder=True`, `reset_by="scan_reset_subjective"`, or `integrity_penalty="target_match_reset"`
- Default (no assessment): score = 0, pass_rate = 0

**Detector payload** (`_build_subjective_detector_payload()` lines 188-215):
```python
{
    "potential": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,      # Base checks (e.g., 4)
    "pass_rate": float,                 # (checks - issues) / checks
    "issues": int,                      # Open finding count
    "weighted_failures": float,         # checks * (1 - pass_rate)
    "assessment_score": float,          # Raw import score
    "placeholder": bool,                # No assessment yet
    "dimension_key": str,               # Normalized name
    "configured_weight": float,         # Dimension weight multiplier
    "components": list,                 # Component labels
    "component_scores": dict,           # Per-component scores
}
```

### **9. VALIDATION & GUARDS**

#### **Preflight checks** (import_cmd.py lines 277-292):
- `--attested-external` + `--manual-override` → Error (mutually exclusive)
- `--attested-external` + `--allow-partial` → Error
- `--manual-override` + `--allow-partial` → Error
- `--manual-override` + (no attest or empty attest) → Error

#### **Skip guard** (lines 370-398):
- If import produced skipped findings (validation failed) and NOT `--allow-partial` → Exit with error
- Forces user to either fix payload or pass `--allow-partial`

#### **Transaction isolation** (import_cmd.py lines 430-473):

2. Run import into working copy
3. Apply policy side-effects
4. Enforce skip guard
5. Append audit event
6. Persist atomically: `state.clear(); state.update(working_state); state_mod.save_state()`

Recorded in `state["assessment_import_audit"]`:

### **KEY INSIGHTS**

1. **Evidence-first subjective scoring**: Open review findings override assessment scores — the import only stores metadata, actual pass-rate is computed from findings.

2. **Provisional vs. durable**: Manual overrides are temporary (provisional until next scan); trusted internal/attested external are durable.

3. **Holistic staleness**: Auto-resolves findings not re-imported, respects dimension scope (full sweep vs. partial).

4. **Mechanical → subjective linkage**: When detectors change, dependent subjective dimensions marked stale for human re-review.

5. **Safe defaults**: Strict validation, fail-closed on partial imports, skip guards, audit trail, attestation requirements.

6. **Concern dismissals**: Dismissed findings create fingerprints stored for suppression in future concern generation.

7. **Multi-source support**: Per-file and holistic imports can coexist; holistic overwrites per-file for assessments.

8. **Cache tracking**: `review_cache` stores content hashes, timestamps, finding counts for each reviewed file — used to detect stale reviews.

## Summary of LLM Integration Patterns in Desloppify

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete LLM integration pattern:

### 1. **Scan Reporting LLM** (`scan_reporting_llm.py`)

**Pattern**: NOT a direct API call. This is **output preparation for agents**.

- The scan reporting system prints structured information to stdout when running in an **agent environment** (detected via `_is_agent_environment()`)
- Detects agent environment through `scan_agent_env.py` (checks `CLAUDE_CODE` or `DESLOPPIFY_AGENT` env vars)
- Outputs scores, dimension table, drag summary, narrative status via `_print_llm_summary()`
- This is **coaching text** read by Claude Code after scan execution, not an LLM API call
- Structure:
  - Score lines (overall, objective, strict, verified)
  - Dimension health table (markdown table)
  - Drag summary (biggest score-impacting dimensions)
  - Stats summary (findings counts, wontfix count, ignore suppression)
  - Workflow guide (how to work with desloppify)
  - Narrative status (headline, strategy hint, top action)

### 2. **Review Preparation** (`prepare.py`, `prepare_batches.py`)

**Pattern**: Data structuring and batching, NOT API calls.

**Key Functions**:
- `prepare_review()` - Prepares per-file review data
  - Loads all files via `lang.file_finder()`
  - Builds review context with dependency graphs
  - Selects files by freshness/staleness (review cache tracking)
  - Returns dict with: dimensions, prompts, context, file requests (with content, zone, neighbors, findings)
  
- `prepare_holistic_review()` - Prepares holistic review batches
  - Builds `HolisticContext` from code analysis (architecture, coupling, conventions, errors, abstractions, testing, API surface, structure, auth, AI debt, migrations)
  - Creates investigation batches via `build_investigation_batches()`
  - Appends design-coherence batch from mechanical concern signals
  - Includes optional issue history context

**Batching Strategy** (`prepare_batches.py`):
- Eight predefined batch functions organizing findings by topic:
  1. Architecture & Coupling (god modules, import-time IO, boundary violations)
  2. Conventions & Errors (sibling behavior outliers, mixed error strategies)
  3. Abstractions & Dependencies (util files, param bags, dep cycles)
  4. Testing & API (critical untested paths, sync/async mix)
  5. Authorization (auth gaps, service role usage)
  6. AI Debt & Migrations (deprecated markers, migration TODOs)
  7. Package Organization (file placement, directory boundaries)
  8. State & Design Integrity (mutable globals, signal density hotspots)
  9. Governance & Contracts (docs/policy vs runtime)

- Each batch collects relevant files from context and wraps with rationale
- Filterable to selected dimensions
- Includes fallback batch for scoped runs

### 3. **Holistic Context Gathering** (`context_holistic/`)

**Pattern**: Multi-phase analysis collecting codebase-wide structure

**Orchestrator** (`orchestrator.py`):
1. Selects files via `select_holistic_files()`
2. Reads file contents with caching
3. Builds context sections in parallel:
   - Architecture (top imported, god modules from lang hook)
   - Coupling (module-level IO from file analysis)
   - Conventions (naming by directory, sibling behavior)
   - Errors (error handling strategy by directory)
   - Abstractions (util files, wrappers, pass-through patterns)
   - Dependencies (cycles, deferred imports)
   - Testing (critical untested paths)
   - API Surface (sync/async mix)
   - Structure (directory profiles, coupling matrix)
4. Enriches with mechanical evidence from state
5. Gathers auth context, AI debt signals, migration signals
6. Normalizes all sections

**Data Sources**:
- File contents (text analysis)
- Dependency graph from lang
- State findings
- Mechanical detector outputs
- Language-specific hooks (architecture_fn, api_surface_fn)

### 4. **Narrative Core** (`narrative/core.py`)

**Pattern**: Pure orchestration computing coaching from state.

**Main Entry**: `compute_narrative(state, context: NarrativeContext)`

**Inputs**:
- State model (findings, scores, history, dimension_scores)
- Optional diff, lang, command, config, plan

**Processing Pipeline**:
1. Load scan history, dimension scores, stats
2. Count open findings by detector (merging structural detectors)
3. Compute phase (first_scan, regression, stagnation, maintenance)
4. Analyze dimensions and debt
5. Detect milestone (progression markers)
6. Build action context and compute actions
7. Compute strategy from findings/actions
8. Compute tools available
9. Compute primary action
10. Generate headline and why_now reasoning
11. Compute verification step
12. Detect risk flags (ignore suppression, wontfix gap)
13. Compute strict target
14. Generate reminders with decay

**Outputs**: `NarrativeResult` dict with:
- phase, headline, dimensions, actions, strategy, tools, debt, milestone
- primary_action, why_now, verification_step, risk_flags, strict_target, reminders

### 5. **File Selection** (`selection.py`)

**Pattern**: Deterministic priority-based file selection for review.

**Algorithm**:
- Filter to production files (skip test/generated/vendor by zone)
- Check review cache for freshness (content hash + reviewed_at timestamp)
- Compute priority score:
  - Base from importer count (high coupling = higher priority)
  - Boost for files with existing findings
  - Penalize low-value files (types, constants, enums, index files < 20 LOC)
- Sort by priority descending
- Cap to max_files if specified

**Staleness Tracking**: Review cache stores:
- content_hash (SHA256 of file content)
- reviewed_at (ISO timestamp)
- Checks against max_age_days threshold

### 6. **Work Queue Building** (`_work_queue/core.py`, `ranking.py`)

**Pattern**: Multi-tier ranking with subjective dimension injection.

**Build Process**:
1. Convert findings to queue items (`build_finding_items`)
   - Filter by status (open/fixed/suppressed)
   - Tag review findings with review_weight
   - Compute effective tier (4 for subjective, otherwise finding tier)
   - Compute subjective scores from dimension scores

2. Sort items (`item_sort_key`):
   - Tier (lower = higher priority)
   - Kind (clusters < findings < subjective)
   - Confidence or subjective score
   - Review weight or finding count
   - ID (tiebreaker)

3. Inject subjective slots (`inject_subjective_slots`)
   - Interleave low-scoring subjective items every N mechanical items
   - Prevents starving subjective dimensions

4. Apply plan ordering (`_apply_plan_order`)
   - Reorder per living plan queue_order
   - Annotate with plan metadata (description, cluster, skip info)
   - Filter to active cluster if specified

**Output**: `WorkQueueResult` with items, tier_counts, fallback info, grouped view

### 7. **LLM Client Abstraction** - THE CRITICAL PATTERN

**The desloppify system does NOT make direct LLM API calls.**

Instead, it uses a **subprocess-based delegation pattern**:

**Via Codex Tool** (`runtime/runner_helpers.py`):
```python
def codex_batch_command(*, prompt: str, repo_root: Path, output_file: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Build one codex exec command line for a batch prompt."""
    effort = os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT", "low").strip().lower()
    return [
        "codex",           # The codex CLI tool (Anthropic's agent framework)
        "exec",            # Execute a prompt
        "--ephemeral",     # One-off execution
        "-C", str(repo_root),
        "-s", "workspace-write",  # Permissions/sandbox mode
        "-c", 'approval_policy="never"',  # Never ask for approval
        "-c", f'model_reasoning_effort="{effort}"',  # Model effort level
        "-o", str(output_file),    # Output JSON to file
        prompt,            # Inline prompt (can be very long string)
    ]
```

**Execution Flow**:
1. Build prompt via `render_batch_prompt()` in `batch_prompt_template.py`
2. Create subprocess command (either via `subprocess.run` or `subprocess.Popen`)
3. Stream stdout/stderr with live logging
4. Implement timeout/stall recovery
5. Parse JSON output from output_file
6. Merge/normalize batch results

**Error Handling**:
- Transient failures (stream disconnects, timeouts) trigger retry with exponential backoff
- Stall detection: monitor output file timestamp and stream activity
- Codex-specific errors (usage limits, auth) detected from stderr patterns
- Parallel execution with ThreadPoolExecutor (configurable max workers)
- Heartbeat logging to track progress

### 8. **Prompt Construction Pattern** (`batch_prompt_template.py`)

**Structure**:
1. **Metadata block**: repo root, packet path, batch index/name, dimensions
2. **Scan evidence note**: explains what mechanical signals are in the blind packet
3. **Seed files block**: files to start investigation from
4. **Historical focus**: previously flagged issues (if enabled)
5. **Mechanical concern signals**: detector hypotheses to confirm/refute
6. **Task requirements**: 13 numbered points
   - Read blind packet and follow system_prompt
   - Handle previous issues and concern signals
   - Think structurally about root causes
   - Explore beyond seed files
   - Return 0-N findings
   - Score/finding consistency
   - Include related_files, dimension, summary, evidence, suggestion, confidence
   - Include impact_scope, fix_scope
   - Include dimension_notes with evidence
   - One decimal place for scores
   - Ignore prior context and assumptions
   - Don't edit files
   - Return ONLY valid JSON
7. **Scope enums**: impact_scope and fix_scope values
8. **Output schema**: exact JSON structure expected

### 9. **State Persistence and Results Flow**

**Input Packet Structure**:
- `command`: "review"
- `mode`: "holistic" (or per-file)
- `language`: lang name
- `dimensions`: list of active dimensions
- `dimension_prompts`: prompt guidance for each dimension
- `lang_guidance`: language-specific notes
- `holistic_context`: full codebase context (architecture, coupling, etc.)
- `system_prompt`: dimension-specific constraints
- `investigation_batches`: the batch array
- `config`: project config (target_strict_score, badge_path, etc.)
- `narrative`: coaching narrative from last scan

**Blind Packet** (what agent sees):
- Same as above but with removed:

3. Validate field requirements
4. Merge across batches (dedup by identifier, combine findings, aggregate assessments)
5. Compute review quality metrics (dimension_coverage, evidence_density, finding_pressure)
6. Persist to state as subjective dimension assessments + findings

### 10. **Integration Points**

**Narrative → Agent**: The narrative computation runs BEFORE batch execution
- Agents see the coaching (phase, why_now, strategy hints) in system_prompt
- But blind packet removes score anchoring to prevent confirmation bias

**Agent → State**: Results merged into state after import
- Subjective dimension scores stored under `dimension_scores`
- Review findings stored with `detector="review"`, `detail.holistic=true` flag
- Historical issue tracking via `review_cache`

**Work Queue → Agents**: Agent results influence next work queue construction
- Review findings appear as T4 (subjective) tier items
- Can be manually marked as reviewed via `investigation` flag
- Failure to investigate tracked and nudged via reminders

### 11. **Key Design Patterns**

1. **Batch Parallelization**: Multiple batches executed in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor
2. **Blind Review**: Agent doesn't see score targets (removed from packet)
3. **Deterministic Inputs**: Prompts/batches reproducible from state and config
4. **File Content Caching**: Optional caching during review preparation to avoid redundant reads
5. **Atomic State Writes**: Output always written via temp+rename pattern
6. **Error Recovery**: Transient failures retried; stalls detected and recovered
7. **Progress Tracking**: Live logs written while agent runs; heartbeat monitoring

### 12. **Synthesis Feature Implications**

For epic synthesis, follow these patterns:

1. **Context Gathering**: Build holistic context just like review does, or reuse existing context
2. **Batching**: Create synthesis-specific batches (e.g., per epic, by dependency, by team ownership)
3. **Prompt Construction**: Follow the `render_batch_prompt()` pattern with dimension focus guidance
4. **Execution**: Use same `run_codex_batch()` infrastructure with custom timeout/effort settings
5. **Output**: Define synthesis-specific JSON schema (e.g., epic structure, dependency ordering, risk flags)
6. **State Integration**: Store synthesis results similarly to review findings (new `detector="epic_synthesis"` perhaps)
7. **Work Queue**: Synthesis findings appear as high-tier items reflecting epic decomposition

The entire system is built around **subprocess delegation to Claude Code agents via the codex tool**, with sophisticated prompt construction, parallel execution, result merging, and state integration.

> DEVELOPER

Design an implementation plan for adding an "epic synthesis" feature to the desloppify CLI tool. This is an LLM-driven step that runs after subjective review findings are imported, clustering findings by root cause into "epics" with coherent theses, resolving contradictions, and ordering by dependency.

## Context / Problem

The tool has a gap between "review findings land" and "agent executes work items." Currently:
1. Review produces independent observations across 20 dimensions (68 findings last run)
2. Auto-clustering groups by dimension/detector mechanically: `auto/review-abstraction_fitness`, `auto/review-design_coherence`, etc.
3. The work queue is a flat list — items that contradict each other coexist (e.g., "add tests for compat layer" alongside "delete compat layer")
4. Executing agents pick items one-by-one without understanding the coherent strategy

The result: agents do mechanical reorganization that doesn't move the score. They follow literal suggestions instead of understanding root causes.

## What Epic Synthesis Does

After review findings land, an LLM step:
1. Reads ALL open findings (review, concerns, mechanical) + current plan state
2. Clusters by ROOT CAUSE, not dimension (e.g., "unnecessary compat layer" groups findings from abstraction_fitness, package_organization, ai_generated_debt)
3. Assigns a THESIS per epic (one-line directive like "Delete the compat/ layer — all callers should import from core directly")
4. Assigns a DIRECTION per epic (enum: delete, merge, flatten, enforce, simplify, decompose)
5. Identifies CONTRADICTIONS and marks one side as superseded
6. Orders epics by dependency (which must come first for others to make sense)
7. Tags epics as agent_safe (boolean) — can an LLM agent execute this without human judgment?

## Existing Infrastructure (from exploration)

### Plan Schema (`engine/_plan/schema.py`)
- PlanModel has: queue_order, skipped, clusters, overrides, superseded, queue_sync_markers
- Cluster TypedDict: name, description, finding_ids, auto, cluster_key, action, user_modified
- SupersededEntry TypedDict: original_id/detector/file/summary, status, candidates, note

### Auto-clustering (`engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py`)
- Groups findings by grouping key: review::dimension, file::detector::path, typed::detector::subtype, etc.
- Auto-generates clusters with `auto/` prefix
- Preserves user-modified clusters
- Entry: `auto_cluster_findings(plan, state) -> int`

### Reconciliation (`engine/_plan/reconcile.py`)
- `reconcile_plan_after_scan(plan, state)` — supersedes disappeared findings, resurfaces stale skips
- Called in `scan_workflow.py`'s `_reconcile_plan_best_effort()`

### Plan Operations (`engine/_plan/operations.py`)
- move_items, skip_items, create_cluster, add_to_cluster, move_cluster, purge_ids, etc.
- Clusters are created via create_cluster() and populated via add_to_cluster()

### Plan Persistence (`engine/_plan/persistence.py`)
- load_plan / save_plan — atomic JSON writes with backup
- Plan validation on load/save

### Scan Workflow Integration (`scan_workflow.py` lines 487-517)
- _reconcile_plan_best_effort: reconcile → sync_unscored → sync_stale → auto_cluster → save
- Best-effort: errors don't fail scan

### Review Import Flow
- Entry: `do_import()` in import_cmd.py — validates, stores assessments, merges findings, persists state
- External: `do_external_submit()` in external.py — validates session, adds provenance, calls do_import
- Holistic: import_holistic_findings → merge_scan(state, review_findings)
- After import: auto-resolves stale findings, updates review cache, appends audit

### LLM Integration Pattern
- Tool does NOT make direct LLM API calls
- Uses subprocess delegation to codex/claude CLI
- Prompt construction: structured text + JSON schema + enumerated requirements
- Output: parsed JSON from file or stdout
- Error handling: retries, stall detection, timeout

### Work Queue (`engine/_work_queue/core.py`)
- build_work_queue: builds ranked list from findings + plan
- collapse_clusters: groups cluster members into single display items
- QueueBuildOptions: tier, cluster, plan, include_skipped, etc.

### CLI Commands
- `plan` subcommands: queue, cluster (create/add/remove/show/list), move, describe, skip, focus, reset
- Cluster rendering: compact table with tier, detector, summary, cluster name

## Design Requirements

1. **New Epic TypedDict** — extends Cluster with: thesis, direction, supersedes, agent_safe, dependency_order, root_cause
2. **New PlanModel field** — `epics: dict[str, Epic]`
3. **Synthesis module** — `engine/_plan/epic_synthesis.py` with prompt building, result parsing, plan mutation
4. **CLI trigger** — `desloppify plan synthesize` subcommand (manual)
5. **Post-import trigger** — optional `--synthesize` flag on review import
6. **Work queue integration** — epics render as collapsed groups, ordered by dependency
7. **Prompt design** — feeds all findings + plan state to LLM, gets back epic definitions
8. **Contradiction resolution** — marks contradicted findings as superseded
9. **Agent compatibility** — output includes agent_safe flag and clear action steps

## Design Constraints

- Follow existing patterns: TypedDict schemas, atomic persistence, best-effort sync
- Epics should coexist with auto-clusters (different prefix, different purpose)
- Don't break existing plan operations (move, skip, focus work with epics too)
- The LLM call must be subprocess-based (codex exec or claude CLI) following existing patterns
- Synthesis should be idempotent — re-running updates existing epics rather than duplicating
- Must work without LLM (degrade gracefully if synthesis fails/skipped)

   108→    deferred: list[str] = plan["deferred"]

   110→    if not deferred:

   113→    for fid in list(deferred):

   116→        skipped[fid] = {

   130→    for cluster in plan["clusters"].values():
   131→        if not isinstance(cluster, dict):

   133→        if not isinstance(cluster.get("finding_ids"), list):
   134→            cluster["finding_ids"] = []
   135→        cluster.setdefault("auto", False)
   136→        cluster.setdefault("cluster_key", "")

   156→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   157→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):

   159→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   160→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")

   162→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   163→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   164→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   165→    if overlap:
   166→        raise ValueError(

   168→        )

   236→        matched_fixer = _subtype_has_fixer(meta, subtype)
   237→        if matched_fixer:
   238→            return f"desloppify fix {matched_fixer} --dry-run"
   239→    elif meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers and not meta.needs_judgment:
   240→        # Pure auto-fix detector, no subtypes
   241→        return f"desloppify fix {meta.fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   242→
   243→    if meta.tool == "move":
   244→        return "desloppify move"
   245→
   246→    # Guidance available — use it (strip examples for subtyped detectors)
   247→    if meta.guidance:
   248→        if subtype:
   249→            return _strip_guidance_examples(meta.guidance)
   250→        return meta.guidance
   251→
   252→    # Final fallback: action_type template
   253→    return _ACTION_TYPE_TEMPLATES.get(
   254→        meta.action_type, "review and fix each finding"
   255→    )
   256→
   257→
   258→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   259→# Main algorithm
   260→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   261→
   262→def _manual_member_ids(clusters: dict[str, dict]) -> set[str]:
   263→    manual_ids: set[str] = set()
   264→    for cluster in clusters.values():
   265→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   266→            manual_ids.update(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   267→    return manual_ids
   268→
   269→
   270→def _group_open_findings(
   271→    findings: dict[str, dict],
   272→    *,
   273→    manual_member_ids: set[str],
   274→) -> tuple[dict[str, list[str]], dict[str, dict]]:
   275→    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   276→    finding_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
   277→    for fid, finding in findings.items():
   278→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
   279→            continue
   280→        if finding.get("suppressed") or fid in manual_member_ids:
   281→            continue
   282→        detector = finding.get("detector", "")
   283→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   284→        key = _grouping_key(finding, meta)
   285→        if key is None:
   286→            continue
   287→        groups[key].append(fid)
   288→        finding_data[fid] = finding
   289→    filtered_groups = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE}
   290→    return filtered_groups, finding_data
   291→
   292→
   293→def _existing_auto_by_key(clusters: dict[str, dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
   294→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str] = {}
   295→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   296→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   297→            continue
   298→        cluster_key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   299→        if cluster_key:
   300→            existing_by_key[cluster_key] = name
   301→    return existing_by_key
   302→
   303→
   304→def _ensure_override_membership(
   305→    plan: PlanModel,
   306→    *,
   307→    member_ids: list[str],
   308→    cluster_name: str,
   309→    now: str,
   310→) -> None:
   311→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   312→    for fid in member_ids:
   313→        if fid not in overrides:
   314→            overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   315→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = cluster_name
   316→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   317→
   318→
   319→def _upsert_group_cluster(
   320→    *,
   321→    key: str,
   322→    member_ids: list[str],
   323→    finding_data: dict[str, dict],
   324→    clusters: dict[str, dict],
   325→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   326→    now: str,
   327→) -> tuple[str, int]:
   328→    cluster_name = _cluster_name_from_key(key)
   329→    rep = finding_data.get(member_ids[0], {})
   330→    detector = rep.get("detector", "")
   331→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   332→    members = [finding_data[fid] for fid in member_ids if fid in finding_data]
   333→    key_parts = key.split("::")
   334→    subtype = key_parts[2] if len(key_parts) >= 3 else None
   335→    description = _generate_description(cluster_name, members, meta, subtype)
   336→    action = _generate_action(meta, subtype)
   337→
   338→    existing_name = existing_by_key.get(key)
   339→    if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   340→        cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   341→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   342→            existing_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   343→            new_ids = [fid for fid in member_ids if fid not in existing_ids]
   344→            if not new_ids:
   345→                return existing_name, 0
   346→            cluster["finding_ids"].extend(new_ids)
   347→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   348→            return existing_name, 1
   349→
   350→        old_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   351→        new_ids = set(member_ids)
   352→        changed = (
   353→            old_ids != new_ids
   354→            or cluster.get("description") != description
   355→            or cluster.get("action") != action
   356→        )
   357→        if not changed:
   358→            return existing_name, 0
   359→        cluster["finding_ids"] = list(member_ids)
   360→        cluster["description"] = description
   361→        cluster["action"] = action
   362→        cluster["updated_at"] = now
   363→        return existing_name, 1
   364→
   365→    if cluster_name in clusters and clusters[cluster_name].get("cluster_key") != key:
   366→        cluster_name = f"{cluster_name}-{len(member_ids)}"
   367→    new_cluster: Cluster = {
   368→        "name": cluster_name,
   369→        "description": description,
   370→        "finding_ids": list(member_ids),
   371→        "created_at": now,
   372→        "updated_at": now,
   373→        "auto": True,
   374→        "cluster_key": key,
   375→        "action": action,
   376→        "user_modified": False,
   377→    }
   378→    clusters[cluster_name] = new_cluster
   379→    existing_by_key[key] = cluster_name
   380→    return cluster_name, 1
   381→
   382→
   383→def _subjective_cluster_payload(
   384→    *,
   385→    queue_ids: list[str],
   386→    description_prefix: str,
   387→) -> tuple[str, str]:
   388→    cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in queue_ids]
   389→    description = f"{description_prefix} {len(queue_ids)} {'unscored' if description_prefix.startswith('Initial') else 'stale'} subjective dimensions"
   390→    action = f"desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {','.join(cli_keys)}"
   391→    return description, action
   392→
   393→
   394→def _sync_subjective_cluster(
   395→    *,
   396→    plan: PlanModel,
   397→    clusters: dict[str, dict],
   398→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   399→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   400→    cluster_key: str,
   401→    cluster_name: str,
   402→    queue_ids: list[str],
   403→    min_size: int,
   404→    description_prefix: str,
   405→    now: str,
   406→) -> int:
   407→    if len(queue_ids) < min_size:
   408→        return 0
   409→    active_auto_keys.add(cluster_key)
   410→    description, action = _subjective_cluster_payload(
   411→        queue_ids=queue_ids,
   412→        description_prefix=description_prefix,
   413→    )
   414→    existing_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key)
   415→    if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   416→        cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   417→        old_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   418→        new_ids = set(queue_ids)
   419→        changed = (
   420→            old_ids != new_ids
   421→            or cluster.get("description") != description
   422→            or cluster.get("action") != action
   423→        )
   424→        if changed:
   425→            cluster["finding_ids"] = queue_ids
   426→            cluster["description"] = description
   427→            cluster["action"] = action
   428→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   429→            _ensure_override_membership(
   430→                plan,
   431→                member_ids=queue_ids,
   432→                cluster_name=existing_name,
   433→                now=now,
   434→            )
   435→            return 1
   436→        _ensure_override_membership(
   437→            plan,
   438→            member_ids=queue_ids,
   439→            cluster_name=existing_name,
   440→            now=now,
   441→        )
   442→        return 0
   443→
   444→    clusters[cluster_name] = {
   445→        "name": cluster_name,
   446→        "description": description,
   447→        "finding_ids": queue_ids,
   448→        "created_at": now,
   449→        "updated_at": now,
   450→        "auto": True,
   451→        "cluster_key": cluster_key,
   452→        "action": action,
   453→        "user_modified": False,
   454→    }
   455→    existing_by_key[cluster_key] = cluster_name
   456→    _ensure_override_membership(
   457→        plan,
   458→        member_ids=queue_ids,
   459→        cluster_name=cluster_name,
   460→        now=now,
   461→    )
   462→    return 1
   463→
   464→
   465→def _delete_stale_auto_clusters(
   466→    *,
   467→    plan: PlanModel,
   468→    clusters: dict[str, dict],
   469→    findings: dict[str, dict],
   470→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   471→    now: str,
   472→) -> int:
   473→    changes = 0
   474→    for name in list(clusters.keys()):
   475→        cluster = clusters[name]
   476→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   477→            continue
   478→        cluster_key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   479→        if cluster_key in active_auto_keys:
   480→            continue
   481→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   482→            alive = [
   483→                fid
   484→                for fid in cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   485→                if fid in findings and findings[fid].get("status") == "open"
   486→            ]
   487→            if alive:
   488→                if len(alive) != len(cluster.get("finding_ids", [])):
   489→                    cluster["finding_ids"] = alive
   490→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   491→                    changes += 1
   492→                continue
   493→        del clusters[name]
   494→        for fid in cluster.get("finding_ids", []):
   495→            override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   496→            if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   497→                override["cluster"] = None
   498→                override["updated_at"] = now
   499→        if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   500→            plan["active_cluster"] = None
   501→        changes += 1
   502→    return changes
   503→
   504→
   505→def auto_cluster_findings(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> int:
   506→    """Regenerate auto-clusters from current open findings."""
   507→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   508→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   509→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   510→    now = utc_now()
   511→
   512→    groups, finding_data = _group_open_findings(
   513→        findings,
   514→        manual_member_ids=_manual_member_ids(clusters),
   515→    )
   516→    [REDACTED](clusters)
   517→    active_auto_keys: set[str] = set()
   518→    changes = 0
   519→
   520→    for key, member_ids in groups.items():
   521→        active_auto_keys.add(key)
   522→        cluster_name, changed = _upsert_group_cluster(
   523→            key=key,
   524→            member_ids=member_ids,
   525→            finding_data=finding_data,
   526→            clusters=clusters,
   527→            existing_by_key=existing_by_key,
   528→            now=now,
   529→        )
   530→        changes += changed
   531→        _ensure_override_membership(
   532→            plan,
   533→            member_ids=member_ids,
   534→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   535→            now=now,
   536→        )
   537→
   538→    all_subjective_ids = sorted(
   539→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []) if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   540→    )
   541→    unscored_state_ids = _current_unscored_ids(state)
   542→    unscored_queue_ids = sorted(
   543→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid in unscored_state_ids
   544→    )
   545→    stale_queue_ids = sorted(
   546→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid not in unscored_state_ids
   547→    )
   548→
   549→    changes += _sync_subjective_cluster(
   550→        plan=plan,
   551→        clusters=clusters,
   552→        existing_by_key=existing_by_key,
   553→        active_auto_keys=active_auto_keys,
   554→        cluster_key=_UNSCORED_KEY,
   555→        cluster_name=_UNSCORED_NAME,
   556→        queue_ids=unscored_queue_ids,
   557→        min_size=_MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE,
   558→        description_prefix="Initial review of",
   559→        now=now,
   560→    )
   561→    changes += _sync_subjective_cluster(
   562→        plan=plan,
   563→        clusters=clusters,
   564→        existing_by_key=existing_by_key,
   565→        active_auto_keys=active_auto_keys,
   566→        cluster_key=_STALE_KEY,
   567→        cluster_name=_STALE_NAME,
   568→        queue_ids=stale_queue_ids,
   569→        min_size=_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE,
   570→        description_prefix="Re-review",
   571→        now=now,
   572→    )
   573→
   574→    changes += _delete_stale_auto_clusters(
   575→        plan=plan,
   576→        clusters=clusters,
   577→        findings=findings,
   578→        active_auto_keys=active_auto_keys,
   579→        now=now,
   580→    )
   581→    plan["updated"] = now
   582→    return changes
   583→

    98→def _resolve_position(
    99→    order: list[str],
   100→    position: str,
   101→    target: str | None = None,
   102→    offset: int | None = None,
   103→    finding_ids: list[str] | None = None,

   105→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
   106→
   107→    *finding_ids* are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
   108→    positions when they already exist in the list.
   109→    """
   110→    moving = set(finding_ids or [])
   111→
   112→    boundary_idx = _resolve_boundary_position(order, position)
   113→    if boundary_idx is not None:
   114→        return boundary_idx
   115→

   117→    if target_idx is not None:

   127→def _resolve_boundary_position(order: list[str], position: str) -> int | None:
   128→    if position == "top":
   129→        return 0
   130→    if position == "bottom":
   131→        return len(order)
   132→    return None
   133→

   135→def _resolve_target_position(
   136→    order: list[str],
   137→    position: str,
   138→    target: str | None,
   139→    moving: set[str],
   140→) -> int | None:
   141→    if position == "before" and target:
   142→        for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
   143→            if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
   144→                return i
   145→        return 0
   146→    if position == "after" and target:
   147→        for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
   148→            if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
   149→                return i + 1
   150→        return len(order)
   151→    return None

   154→def _resolve_shift_position(
   155→    order: list[str],
   156→    position: str,
   157→    offset: int | None,
   158→    finding_ids: list[str] | None,
   159→    moving: set[str],
   160→) -> int | None:
   161→    if position not in {"up", "down"} or offset is None:
   162→        return None
   163→
   164→    if not finding_ids:
